packages.changelog:
Study streak and time estimate, backups you can restore on the console,
in-app updates, larger card text on a TV, and a clearer whiteboard.
Verified on hardware; updating from inside the app is first exercised by
updating to this release from 0.3.0 builds that have the update check.

- Deck list: the header shows about how long today's cards will take
  ("19 cards due · about 12 min", from your pace over the last 30 days),
  and the status line a study streak on the right (days in a row with
  reviews; today counts once you have studied).
- Settings > Collection: Check Database (Anki's), Back up now, and Restore
  from backup (a list of the backups by date; the current collection is
  backed up first and the next sync asks which side to keep, as in Anki).
  Backups made in the same second no longer overwrite each other.
- Updates: the app checks GitHub for a newer release when it opens (this
  can be turned off in Settings > About) and says so; Settings > About >
  Updates downloads the new .nro with progress, and it replaces the old one
  when AnkiNX exits.
- On a TV (docked), card text is a size larger by default (Settings >
  Study > On a TV: same, 125%, 150%), on top of each deck's zoom; it
  follows docking and undocking while studying.
- Whiteboard easier to recognise: the pen and bin icons (which read as
  "edit card" and "delete card") are now labelled pills, "Draw" with a brush
  and "Clear"; Draw fills blue and the card gets a blue outline while
  drawing, and the first time a hint says that you can draw anywhere on the
  card (scrolling is paused meanwhile).
- Replay on the answer side plays the question's audio first, then the
  answer's, as Anki does, unless the deck has "Skip question when replaying
  answer" (that option was editable but not applied).

packages.name: atmosphere
packages.title: atmosphere
packages.author: atmosphere-nx
packages.description: Atmosphère is a work-in-progress customized firmware for the Nintendo Switch.
packages.details:
Atmosphère is a work-in-progress customized firmware for the Nintendo Switch.

https://github.com/atmosphere-nx/atmosphere
packages.changelog:
**1.12.1** is Atmosphère's ninety-fourth official release.

**Please be sure to update fusee when upgrading to 1.12.1**. fusee-primary no longer exists, and will not work any more.

With thanks to the @switchbrew team, Atmosphère 1.12.1 is bundled with [hbl](https://github.com/switchbrew/nx-hbloader) 2.4.5, and [hbmenu](https://github.com/switchbrew/nx-hbmenu) 3.6.1.

The following was changed since the last release:
* Support was added for the new c-ares resolver in `dns.mitm`.
  * Firmware 23.0.0 introduced a new set of commands to the `sfdnsres` service. These commands provide c-ares async support for DNS resolution and are now used by most sysmodules.
  * This resulted in host redirection not being applied at all and without warning since we simply were not intercepting the new commands.
  * `dns.mitm` now fully reimplements the c-ares serialization code and intercepts the relevant commands. In tandem with the `bsdsocket` sysmodule, we now keep track of resolution queries and redirect their results. 
* Support was added for the new "BatchRead" storage in `fs.mitm`.
  * Firmware 23.0.0 introduced a new type of filesystem storage object abstracted by the interface "IStorageForBatchRead". This is a derived class from "IStorage" with the purpose of adding the new "BatchRead" command.
  * Anything that uses the filesystem API now attempts to use this type of storage instead of the old one. This is of particular relevance for `qlaunch` and for supporting custom themes which were broken as a consequence of this change.
  * `fs.mitm` was updated and extended to not only support the new storage type but also intercept a few newer commands that were previously missing.
* The patches for the browser applets were redesigned.
  * The introduction of these patches in the previous release led to several issues and crashes, notably during media playback in the eshop and within games that use LibAppletOff.
  * After extensive analysis and testing it was concluded that the browser applets were running out of memory and still required reducing the memory we reserve for custom sysmodules.
  * New patches have been devised and introduced in this release.
    * Instead of patching size checks, we now trick the browser applets into thinking there is 1GB of free memory available to them.
    * Unused memory is still being reclaimed and discounted from the root heap, but now more realistically.
    * The browser engine's heap is now being shrunk with no noticeable downsides to media playback nor web page rendering.
  * Thanks to these changes we can now provide 40MB for custom system modules once again.
* A number of minor issues were fixed and improvements were made, such as:
  * Automatic PRODINFO backup was fixed for recent console models that no longer use the ECC device certificate (thanks @chrisbraucker).
  * State initialization for SharedMemory and TransferMemory was fixed (thanks @fl0be).
  * Compatibility was fixed for Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter (thanks @masagrator). 
* General system stability improvements to enhance the user's experience.

And the following was changed in 1.12.0:
* Support was added for 23.0.0.
* Special thanks to @alula for handling the implementation of several kernel changes.
    * The console should boot and atmosphère should be fully functional.
    * **Please note**: As a result of changes made to nintendo's software in 23.0.0, there is even less memory available for custom system modules.
        * The amount of memory we can steal from the applet pool has been reduced beyond 7MB and we can no longer launch browser applets (e.g.: eshop) without crashing.
        * To compensate for this, a set of patches for the browser applets has been introduced.
            * Thanks to the redesign of the browser applets in 22.0.0 there are only 3 applets we need to worry about: systemWeb, openWeb and LibAppletOff.
            * With the added burden of maintaining patches for these app

packages.changelog:
This is an UNOFFICIAL, UNSUPPORT Atmosphere fork. Do not report any issues with this to Atmosphere maintainers

- Support for booting from eMMC
  - Fusee will check for a FAT32 filesystem on eMMC BOOT1 (at 1MB offset), eMMC BOOT1 (at 0MB offset), and eMMC GPP partition, any SD card partition. It will pick the first one it finds that does not have a .no_boot_storage file in the root directory
- Support for emuSD
  - Allows redirecting all SD accesses in HOS to a separate file or partition on the SD card or eMMC. Note: HOS will crash, if no physical SD card is inserted
  - emuSD configuration is read from /emusd/emusd.ini with the following format:
```
[emusd]
enabled=[1 for SD card | 4 for eMMC]
sector=[start sector of emuSD partition]
path=[path to emusd file]
```
- For eMMC file based emuSD, the file is read from the first available FAT32 partition on eMMC
- Support for emuMMC on eMMC
  - Allows creating file or partition based emuMMC on the eMMC
  - emuMMC configuration is read from /emummc/emummc.ini with the following format:
```
[emummc]
enabled=[1 for SD card | 4 for eMMC]
sector=[start sector of emuMMC partition]
path=[path to emuMMC file]
nintendo_path=[path to Nintendo folder]
id=[emuMMC id]
```
- For eMMC file based emuMMC, the file is read from the first available FAT32 partition on eMMC

**Install:** delete old autorun installation, unzip `autorun-test-build-4.zip` to the **root of your SD card** — everything goes into `switch/wine`. 

**What changed, how to upgrade from test-build-3 and known issues:** see the release thread on the forum:
[https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/101/autorun-test-build-4](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/101/autorun-test-build-4)

Upgrading from test-build-3? Your Windows user folder is now `C:\users\steamuser` (was `C:\users\wine`): move saves and settings from `switch/wine/drive_c/users/wine` to `switch/wine/drive_c/users/steamuser`. The forum post has the details.

Game reports and help: [Game Discussion](https://forum.ticoverse.com/category/21/game-discussion) · [Help & Suggestions](https://forum.ticoverse.com/category/23/help-suggestions)

### Antivirus false positives

Some of the DLLs in this package are heavily patched Wine builds, modified so Wine can run on the Switch's OS at all. This can trip antivirus and scanner heuristics. That's a false positive caused by the patching, not malicious code — the source is in this repository if you want to check it or build it yourself.

packages.changelog:
**BedrockLink is now BetterBedrock NX: a Minecraft (Bedrock) toolkit for a modded Switch.**

**New: Vibrant Visuals on a Switch 1** (Minecraft 1.26.44)
- The original Switch's Minecraft has Vibrant Visuals built in but switched off; BetterBedrock NX switches it on (an Atmosphère exefs patch for that exact build - other versions just don't get it).
- **Fast / Balanced / Quality** profiles tuned for the Switch 1: lower resolutions (480p-720p), lighter shadows redrawn every 2nd frame, shorter Vibrant Visuals distance. They work without the preset menu the Switch 1 version lacks.
- Needs an overclock: on a Mariko Switch in handheld at a high overclock it ran at 20-25 fps with Mojang's own settings; the profiles are lighter than those. Not playable at stock clocks.
- How it works and exactly what it changes: docs/vibrant-visuals.md.

**Also new**
- Two pages, switched with L/R: **Online** (Microsoft sign-in fix, your own server - as before) and **Graphics**.
- New name, new logo.

**Upgrading from BedrockLink:** unzip over your SD card. Your server settings carry over; the first start removes the old BedrockLink app and overlay files (no duplicate overlay). The old `/switch/BedrockLink` folder (log, backups) can be deleted.

**Install:** unzip `BetterBedrockNX-2.0.0.zip` to the root of the SD card.

**Tested on:** Switch (Mariko), firmware 22.5.0, Atmosphère 1.11.2, emuMMC, Minecraft 1.26.44, Nextendo Prelude 3.5.5 and 3.5.11, Horizon OC.

Joining through BedrockConnect means its server sees your gamertag, like any server you join. See the README for details and privacy notes.

packages.details:
Bomberman 64 for Nintendo Switch — native homebrew port (.nro) of BM64Recomp via N64Recomp static recompilation, rendered with libultraship (OpenGL). Bring your own ROM.

https://github.com/paulodiasred/BM64Switch
packages.changelog:
**Bomberman 64: Recompiled for Nintendo Switch** — first release. Nintendo Switch port by [Paulo Dias](https://github.com/paulodiasred).

**[Português abaixo](#português)**

A native Nintendo Switch port of [Bomberman 64: Recompiled](https://github.com/RevoSucks/BM64Recomp) (N64Recomp static recompilation, rendered with libultraship over OpenGL).

**You need your own Bomberman 64 (USA) ROM. It is not included.**

### Features
- Runs natively on the Switch at 60 FPS, with audio, saves and rumble.
- Installable NSP with an icon on the HOME menu, or a plain NRO for the Homebrew Menu.
- In-game settings menu (press **−**): language, resolution, anti-aliasing, VSync, CPU clock, controls and cheats.
- **Portuguese (Brazil) translation**: menus and game text, plus all 33 Adventure conversations.

### Install
1. **NSP (recommended):** install `BM64Recompiled-v1.0.0.nsp` with DBI, Tinfoil or Goldleaf. Installing NSPs requires sigpatches in Atmosphère. Then open it from the HOME menu.
   **NRO:** copy `BM64Recompiled-v1.0.0.nro` to `sdmc:/switch/` and open it from the Homebrew Menu while holding **R** on a game (title override). The album (applet mode) doesn't have enough memory.
2. Put your ROM (`.z64`, `.n64` or `.v64`, any name) in `sdmc:/switch/bm64recomp/`, `sdmc:/switch/` or the root of the SD card.
3. Portuguese: **−** → **General** → **Language / Idioma**.

Saves and settings are kept in `sdmc:/switch/bm64recomp/` and shared between the NSP and the NRO.

---

### Português

Port nativo para Nintendo Switch do [Bomberman 64: Recompiled](https://github.com/RevoSucks/BM64Recomp). Ele usa recompilação estática com N64Recomp e renderização com libultraship sobre OpenGL. Port feito por [Paulo Dias](https://github.com/paulodiasred).

**É preciso ter a sua própria ROM do Bomberman 64 (USA). Ela não vem incluída.**

### Recursos
- Roda nativo no Switch a 60 FPS, com som, saves e vibração.
- NSP instalável, com ícone na tela inicial, ou NRO para o Homebrew Menu.
- Menu de configurações no jogo (aperte **−**). Tem idioma, resolução, anti-aliasing, VSync, clock da CPU, controles e cheats.
- **Tradução para português do Brasil**: menus e textos do jogo, mais as 33 conversas do modo Aventura.

### Instalação
1. Escolha uma das duas versões:
   - **NSP (recomendado):** instale o `BM64Recompiled-v1.0.0.nsp` pelo DBI, Tinfoil ou Goldleaf (é preciso ter sigpatches no Atmosphère). Depois abra pela tela inicial.
   - **NRO:** copie o `BM64Recompiled-v1.0.0.nro` para `sdmc:/switch/` e abra pelo Homebrew Menu segurando **R** ao abrir um jogo (title override). Pelo Álbum não há memória suficiente.
2. Coloque a sua ROM (`.z64`, `.n64` ou `.v64`, com qualquer nome) em um destes lugares:
   - `sdmc:/switch/bm64recomp/`;
   - `sdmc:/switch/`;
   - a raiz do cartão SD.
3. Para jogar em português: **−** → **General** → **Language / Idioma**.

Os saves e as configurações ficam em `sdmc:/switch/bm64recomp/`, e o NSP e o NRO usam a mesma pasta.

---

### MAJOR RELEASE (1.1.0)

- Added support for the V.Smile Motion controller (closing the biggest remaining gap in the console library), the Smart Keyboard, and the Jammin' Gym Class dance mat, configurable in Settings > Controller
  - V.Smile Motion uses the Switch controller's motion sensors (Handheld, Pro Controller, or a Joy-Con pair). Tilt, swing, and shake gestures are all supported
  - Two-player Motion is supported, but input is a little less precise when both players use Motion controllers: each controller's report rate had to be halved to stop the extra traffic from dropping inputs
  - Smart Keyboard uses a USB keyboard plugged into the Switch (US, UK, French, German, and Spanish layouts)
- Added real standby (power off) support. Quitting from the pause menu now turns the console off like its OFF button (the game's "goodbye" audio plays) and keeps that state, so the next launch of that game picks up where you left off
  - Some games keep your progress in the console's memory during standby rather than on the cartridge (e.g. Shrek: Dragon's Tale's "Continue" option in Learning Adventure), so that now works across sessions
  - **Quitting any other way (L+R+Plus or HOME) skips this, the same as pulling the cartridge without pressing OFF**, so keep that in mind
  - Optional Console ON / OFF / RESTART button binds, and the pause menu's Reset Game now acts as the console's RESTART button
- Added support for the joystick's different tilt levels (translated from the left analog stick; the D-Pad is still full tilt)
- Minor additional system settings: boot into the BIOS with no cartridge, the BIOS test screen, PAL / NTSC video mode, a color-button controller LED overlay, and the skip-VTech-logo jumper
- Save states now remember the console setup they were made on (console type, region, logo jumper), so loading one after changing those settings won't restart the game
- Fixed the emulated V.Smile Motion console reporting itself to games as a Cyber Pocket
- The US V.Smile Motion BIOS is now correctly identified as v1.03 (it really boots with the standard V.Smile intro), with the matching Region labels and BIOS test screen

Some of the DLLs in this package are heavily patched Wine builds, modified so Wine can run on the Switch's OS at all. This can trip antivirus and scanner heuristics. packages.changelog:
### What's new in 1.1.0
- **16:9 widescreen** (on by default). More of the road and scenery at the sides; the HUD stays centred. Switch back any time in the menu (`+` and `-` together) under **SCREEN: 16:9 / 4:3**.
  - The race sky is stretched across the full width, so the clouds reach the screen edges.
  - 2D screens ("Gentlemen, start your engines", Mission Select) get black side bars.
  - With 16:9 the game draws every scenery block around the car, so grandstands and trees no longer cut off at the sides.
- **Faster renderer**: the picture is drawn on the worker cores while the next frame runs. Tested on hardware: locked **57.52 FPS** through full races at 16:9.
- **New shift buttons**: shift up is now **X** and shift down is **B**. The bumper and cockpit views moved to **L** and **R**.

### Installation
No ROMs or copyrighted game files are included. You must supply your own copy of the arcade ROM set.

```text
sdmc:/switch/daytona/
├── daytona.nro
└── daytona.zip
```
1. Copy `daytona.nro` (or extract the zip) to `sdmc:/switch/daytona/`, replacing the old one.
2. Place your MAME `daytona.zip` (Revision A) in the same folder.
3. Launch from the Homebrew Menu (title override recommended for full memory).

### Controls
| Action | Input |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Steer** | Left Analog Stick (or D-Pad Left/Right) |
| **Accelerate** | `ZR` or Right Stick Up |
| **Brake** | `ZL` or Right Stick Down |
| **Shift Up / Down** | `X` / `B` |
| **Direct Gear Selection** | D-Pad Up (Gear 4) / Down (Gear 1) |
| **VR Cameras** | `L` (Bumper), `A` (Chase), `Y` (Far), `R` (Cockpit) |
| **Start / Coin** | `+` (Start), `-` (Coin) |
| **Pause Menu** | `+` and `-` pressed together |
| **Test / Service** | `L3` (Test switch) / `R3` (Service coin) |
| **Test menu cursor** | `R` (Up) / `L` (Down) |

packages.changelog:
### 🌍 DBI Multilingual Localization (v0.0.105)
![GitHub release (tag)](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/rashevskyv/DBIPatcher/912/total)

This release provides translations for **DBI version 912**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Use the `DBI.nro` and the `translation_XX.bin` files **from this release together**. The translation tables now carry a lookup index that older patched `DBI.nro` builds do not read.

### ✨ What's new
- **DBI 912 support.** The runtime-translation engine is now part of this repository (`vendor/dbi_translate`, originally [0xroast/dbi-translate](https://github.com/0xroast/dbi-translate)) and supports DBI 905 and 912.
- **Smooth menus.** Translation lookups use a hash index instead of scanning the whole table for every line. Menus, context menus and settings no longer lag ([#28](https://github.com/rashevskyv/DBIPatcher/issues/28)).
- **More stable patch.** The patcher no longer keeps its state on top of DBI's own text buffers, which could corrupt some lines and reload the table.
- **Game info panel translated** — tabs (Content / Tickets / Saves) and the Name / Author / Version / Language rows ([#25](https://github.com/rashevskyv/DBIPatcher/issues/25)).
- **Clean Cyrillic translations.** Ukrainian, Belarusian and Kazakh no longer get mixed words such as "Такмпити" or cut words such as "Видалит" in context menus.
- **Version line** at the top shows the translation language, e.g. `912-ua`.
- **New DBI 912 strings** translated for all languages: transfer progress lines, theme menu, panel hints, total play time.

### ✨ Cyrillic glyph repair
The bundled `DBI.nro` repairs the embedded glyphs `Є/є`, `І/і`, and `Ї/ї` used by Ukrainian, Belarusian, and Kazakh translations.

### 📦 Supported Languages
*   **BE** — Belarusian
*   **DE** — German
*   **EN** — English (US)
*   **ENGB** — English (UK)
*   **ES** — Spanish (Spain)
*   **ES419** — Spanish (Latin America)
*   **ET** — Estonian
*   **FR** — French
*   **FRCA** — French (Canada)
*   **ID** — Indonesian
*   **IT** — Italian
*   **JP** — Japanese
*   **KK** — Kazakh
*   **KR** — Korean
*   **LT** — Lithuanian
*   **LV** — Latvian
*   **NL** — Dutch
*   **PL** — Polish
*   **PT** — Portuguese (Portugal)
*   **PTBR** — Portuguese (Brazil)
*   **UA** — Ukrainian
*   **ZHCN** — Chinese (Simplified)
*   **ZHTW** — Chinese (Traditional)
*   **TR** — Turkish

***

### 🛠️ Installation Instruction
1. Download **`DBI.nro`** (Patched/Compatible version) from this release.
2. Download the **`translation_XX.bin`** file for your desired language.
3. **Rename** the translation file to exactly `translation.bin`.
4. Place both `DBI.nro` and `translation.bin` into the `/switch/DBI/` folder on your SD card.

### 📝 Translation Coverage
This community translation set is still evolving. Some strings may remain untranslated and appear in the original DBI language or use an English fallback. Please report missing or incorrect strings in the project issues.

### 🙏 Credits
- [Bohdan Buinich](https://github.com/BohdanBuinich) — creator of the earlier `dbi-i18n` runtime-translation approach, compatible table format, and Cyrillic font-glyph repair approach.
- [0xroast](https://github.com/0xroast) — author of `dbi-translate`, the runtime patcher this project now includes and extends.

packages.changelog:
Fixes the textures that went black after a long session, and makes 60 fps Interpolated smoother while running.

### What's new since v1.1.1

- **Textures no longer go black or noisy after playing a while.** The Switch's GPU service (nvdrv) keeps one record per texture in a memory area that libnx sizes at 8 MiB. GLideN64 keeps up to 8,000 textures, and past about 5,000 every new texture failed to load (GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY), which showed as black or noisy surfaces until the game was restarted. The area is now 32 MiB. On the console, a tour of seven levels with the texture cache full (8,000 textures, more than 10,000 created) gave no error, where the old build failed from 5,200 textures.

- **Resolution 4x (1080p, experimental):** 1280x960 drawn into a 1920x1080 picture, 16:9 kept, for a docked console. It costs more GPU time and was measured at 1428 MHz only. Settings > Display > Resolution, then Restart Game.

- **Dev Tools > Warp** now waits for a loaded file: a warp from the intro left the main menu without input.

packages.changelog:
# Emulanders 1.0.1

Maintenance release. No change to the sysmodule's behaviour; the main changes are in Emulanders Portal and the overlay translations.

## Changes

### Emulanders Portal
- Language support expanded from 2 to 10: English, Portuguese (Brazil), Spanish, French, German, Italian, Russian, Korean, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese. The selection is stored in `sdmc:/emulanders/config.json` and shared with the overlay.
- Buttons now size themselves to their label, and the language and theme lists wrap onto a new row, so longer translations no longer overflow.
- Cyrillic and CJK text is rendered with the console's shared system fonts.
- Figure Image Editor: the `Figures / Scans / Favorites` and `Menu / Back` buttons are on a single row, and the step header is one line instead of three. This gives the figure and photo lists roughly 95 px of extra height (about seven visible rows instead of four).
- Figure Image Editor (Step 3 Crop Tool): tuned live preview sizing and button heights so `(B) Back to Photos` has generous vertical clearance and is never clipped by the bottom status bar in 720p handheld mode.
- Download failures (no network, bad URL) are reported instead of silently extracting an empty archive.
- Fixed controller hot-plugging when docking and undocking, and resizing between 720p and 1080p.

### Tesla overlay
- All 10 languages are fully translated (previously only English and Portuguese were).
- Reads the language chosen in the Portal; falls back to the system language otherwise.
- Fixed the version-mismatch warning, which was being overwritten and never shown.

### Sysmodule
- Fixed a possible panic when the debug log was trimmed in the middle of a multi-byte character (for example accented figure names).

## Packages

| File | Contents |
|:--|:--|
| `Emulanders-Bundle-1.0.1.zip` | Everything: sysmodule, overlay, Portal and language files. Extract to the SD card root. |
| `Emulanders-Portal-1.0.1.zip` | Portal only (`switch/EmulandersPortal/`). |
| `Emulanders-Core-1.0.1.zip` | Sysmodule and overlay only. |
| `emulanders_assets_pack.zip` | Portrait pack (unchanged, from 1.0.0). |

## Upgrading from 1.0.0
Extract the bundle over the existing install and restart the console. Figures, assets and settings are kept. The sysmodule and overlay must be updated together; the overlay warns if their versions differ.

## Compatibility
Fully verified and tested on **Firmware 23.0.1 with Atmosphère 1.12.1** (CNX 23.0.1-1) and Firmware 22.1 with Atmosphère 1.11.1. Full hardware validation confirmed for `nfc:mf:u` protocol emulation, physical Joy-Con Mifare tag dumping, Tesla Overlay hot-swapping, and in-game figure write-back. Compatible with all firmwares 4.0.0+.

## Credits
- XorTroll and Emuiibo contributors (Subv, ogniK, averne, spx01, SciresM): original sysmodule architecture and `nfp-mitm` research.
- libtesla developers (AD2076, AmonRaNet): overlay framework.
- Switchbrew and the aarch64-switch-rs team: libnx and the Rust bindings.
- Skylanders community: research on the figure format.

See YAML pipelines for reference. - Drag the installation files into a new folder called `fallout1` in your `switch` folder on the root of your SD card. You can also put `fallout1` on the root of your SD card. - Put the necessary executable in your `switch` folder on the root of your SD card, either `.nro` or `.nso`. ## Changes compared to previous release ### Performance & stability - Faster loading. Art assets are pre-cached at startup, so maps, saves and area transitions load quicker. Note that initial load will be a bit longer. I would expect less stutter if any also. - Runtime diagnostics overlay. Press L+R+Right Stick Click for live FPS, frame time, memory usage and startup load timing. More a curio than useful to average person using this, but at least you can tell me if there's bad framerate somewhere! ### Controls - **L shoulder button now toggles active item, to stop using the cursor to do it. Should make switching items much, much smoother.** - Pressing the left stick now opens the native keyboard when a text input field is present. Otherwise, it's stealth mode. - No more accidental double-triggers on menus, inventory, the Skilldex and quick save/load. ### Native keyboard - Character names, save names and search dialogs all use the Switch software keyboard, sorry about this not being included on initial release. - Item quantity dialogs use a dedicated numeric keypad instead of increment and decrement buttons. - The "Ask About" dialog for dialogue with NPCs opens the keyboard automatically. ### Save compatibility - Save files from the PC version of Fallout 1 CE generally work on Switch now, and Switch saves work back on PC. Some heavily modded or unusual saves may still fail to load. **This is experimental.** - Make backups before moving saves between platforms. ### Setup and configuration - `fallout1_nx.ini` is created automatically on first launch with sensible defaults. - Introduced `fallout1` fallback folder on root of SD card, like the Fallout 2 port. [Fallout 2 port that I've also worked on. (similar QOL updates soon!)](https://github.com/ryandeering/fallout2-ce-switch/releases/latest) Thank you for your patience and enjoy. packages.changelog:
# Golden Balloon NX v1.2.1-nx1

This update focuses on **save support, stability, and Nintendo Switch performance**.

## Highlights

### 💾 Save & configuration fixes

* Fixed save data handling on Nintendo Switch.
* Adventure progress can now be stored correctly on the SD card.
* Configuration/settings persistence has also been improved.
* Save data and configuration are stored under:
  `sdmc:/switch/goldenballoon/`

If you are upgrading from the previous release, you can keep your existing `save/` folder and `mdkr64.ini` and simply replace `goldenballoon.nro`.

### ⚡ Major Switch performance improvements

* Removed a redundant offscreen framebuffer path from normal Switch gameplay.
* Removed an unnecessary full-screen framebuffer blit that was still being performed even when the game was already rendering at native Switch resolution.
* Switch now reports the actual effective 1x render scale to the OpenGL backend instead of retaining Golden Balloon's desktop-oriented 2x supersampling setting.
* Disabled an unused framebuffer-memory compatibility path by default on Switch.
* Added GCC Link-Time Optimization (LTO) for the Switch build.
* Improved performance and frame consistency, especially in heavier areas such as the Adventure Mode hub worlds.
* These optimizations do **not** reduce the normal 1280×720 output resolution.

### 🔊 Audio

* Includes the Switch-specific audio buffering improvements designed to reduce underruns and crackling.
* The game's original audio synthesis rate, music timing, and pitch remain unchanged.

## Installation

Copy:

`goldenballoon.nro`

to:

`sdmc:/switch/goldenballoon/`

A legally dumped **Diddy Kong Racing US 1.1** ROM is required:

`baserom.us.v80.z64`

Place it in the same Golden Balloon folder.

> **No ROM, copyrighted game assets, or Nintendo/Rare game data are included with this release.**

## Notes

Golden Balloon NX is still under active development. Further Switch-specific CPU/GPU optimizations and presentation improvements are being investigated.

Thanks to everyone testing the port and reporting issues! ❤️

packages.changelog:
## 🌋 Vulkan Hardware Acceleration
- **Native Vulkan Backend:** High-performance Vulkan rendering on the Tegra X1 Maxwell GPU via Horizon OS display subsystem (`vi`/`NWindow`).
- **Massive Performance Boost:** Significantly smoother framerates and drastically reduced frame-time latency compared to OpenGL, especially when running intensive gameplay mods like *Brutal Doom*.
- **Dynamic Light Optimization:** Completely eliminated GPU hangs and stalls when loading dynamic light buffers.
- **Credit:** Immense credit and special thanks to **[NaGa](https://github.com/NaGaa95)** for developing the Vulkan driver for Nintendo Switch!

## 🎼 Soundfont Support (.sf2) & Setup
- **Direct Soundfont Selector:** You can now choose your active soundfont directly inside the game! Go to `Options -> Sound Options -> Soundfont`.
- **Auto-Detection:** GZDoom automatically scans `sdmc:/switch/gzdoom/soundfonts/` and loads external soundfonts seamlessly.
- **Supported Synthesizers:** Upgraded **FluidSynth** and **Timidity++** engines.

### How to Use Soundfonts:
1. Place your `.sf2` files into `sdmc:/switch/gzdoom/soundfonts/` (e.g., `AweROMGM.sf2`, `SC-55.sf2`, `FluidR3_GM.sf2`, `gzdoom.sf2`).
2. In-game, open **Options** -> **Sound Options**.
3. Set **MIDI Device** to **FluidSynth** (or **Timidity++**).
4. Select your preferred soundfont from the **Soundfont** option list.

## 📦 Package Contents
- `gzdoom.nro` (Vulkan-enabled GZDoom 4.14.2 binary)
- `gzdoom.pk3`, `brightmaps.pk3`, `game_widescreen_gfx.pk3`, `game_support.pk3`, `lights.pk3`
- `gzdoom_launcher.nro` (Mod / IWAD selector)
- Default soundfonts & FM sound banks

## Installation
Extract `gzdoom_2026_switch_release.zip` to the root of your SD card (`sdmc:/switch/gzdoom/`). Place IWADs in `iwads/` and mods in `pwads/`.
Extraxt the `extract.this.too.zip` to the root of your SD card for OTHER necessary files.

I've included my recommended `gzdoom.ini` file which enabled autorun and turns off vertical look with the right analog stick.

Additionally I have include an edited Brutal Doom v21(The most recent full release), which allows vertical auto aim, so you don't need to use mouse look to shoot up and down. As well as removing recoil from weapons so you'll never have to adjust the camera.
Just the way Carmack Intended!

---

❤️ **Enjoying the port?**
If this project helped you out, consider [buying me a coffee on Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/thorhax) or supporting on [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/c/Thorhax) to support future updates!

packages.changelog:
PCSX2 on Nintendo Switch — **Vulkan/NVK** branch (separate lineage from the deko3d `master`).

### Highlights
- **Vulkan GS renderer (`GSDeviceVK`)** running on the switch-nvk (NVK/Mesa) driver, replacing the hand-written deko3d path. Loaderless ICD bootstrap, zero-copy `VK_NN_vi_surface` WSI, runtime TFX shader compile.
- **FastmemLite identity-map fix** — keeps the EE fast path enabled across identity TLB maps of the low 32MB instead of disabling on any TLB write (big EE perf win for games that identity-map, e.g. to set a cache mode).
- Reverted the AArch64 vector-register-file expansion (it regressed FPS via the MTVU sync stub on this hardware).
- Docker build + nxlink deploy tooling.

### Install (clean Switch)
1. Copy `armsx2nx.nro` to `sdmc:/switch/`.
2. Put your **PS2 BIOS** dump in `sdmc:/switch/armsx2/bios/` (required, not bundled).
3. Put game ISOs in `sdmc:/switch/armsx2/games/`.
Resources/shaders/driver are bundled in the NRO and self-extract on first boot.

> WARNING - untested-on-hardware: the FastmemLite identity-map change is correct by construction but still needs on-device validation per game.

Built from branch vulkan-nvk @ 45d51127.

## How Many Dudes? NX v1.0.0

The first public release of the unofficial **How Many Dudes? Android wrapper for Nintendo Switch**.

This port runs the original Android ARM64 GameMaker runner natively through a lightweight Android/JNI compatibility layer.

### Features

- Fully playable gameplay
- Touch-screen controls
- ASTC texture rendering
- Native audio playback
- In-game cutscene support
- Local saves and preferences
- Suspend and resume support
- Optimized performance during high-unit-count battles
- Automatic handheld and docked resolutions
- Built-in crash and performance logging

### Controls

This game is designed around tapping, dragging, and direct unit placement. Therefore, this port intentionally uses the Nintendo Switch touch screen.

**Handheld mode is required for practical gameplay.** Joy-Con and Pro Controller controls are not currently supported.

### Installation

This release does not include any copyrighted game files.

You need a legally obtained Android ARM64 APK of **How Many Dudes?**, specifically build `100.0.890` (`com.bscotch.hmd`).

From the APK, extract:

- `lib/arm64-v8a/libyoyo.so`
- The complete `assets/` folder
- The APK itself, renamed to `game.apk`

Place everything on your SD card as follows:

```text
sdmc:/switch/hmd_nx/
├── hmd_nx.nro
├── libyoyo.so
├── game.apk
└── assets/
    ├── game.droid
    └── ...
```

Launch the Homebrew Menu using a full title override by holding **R** while opening an installed game. Applet/Album mode is not supported.

See the repository README for automatic Windows setup and complete instructions.

### Limitations

- Google Play Games, cloud saves, achievements, billing, ads, and Android in-app updates are unavailable.
- Other APK versions may use a different GameMaker runner and are not guaranteed to work.
- Controller input is not implemented.

### NRO Checksum

SHA-256:

```text
8CA8DFF643C3AC9DFA97C9710887459E23ED035E6C016F71A1FC9F3C14E45EA0
```

### Legal

This is an unofficial compatibility wrapper. No APK, game code, `libyoyo.so`, `game.droid`, or other original asset is included.

**How Many Dudes?** and its assets belong to Butterscotch Shenanigans and their respective rightsholders. Users must obtain the original game legally.

packages.changelog:
**Kirikiroid2-NX v1.0.1** — compatibility fixes.

### What's new
- **windowEx plugin** added (the Android APK has it built in). Games that call `Window.registerExEvent()` and other windowEx methods no longer stop with *Member "registerExEvent" does not exist* — e.g. **Ninki Seiyuu: How to Make a Pop Voice Actress** (#1).
- **Modal dialogs close properly.** A dialog opened with `showModal()` is now hidden when it closes. Before, a game's own dialog (e.g. Ninki Seiyuu's language selection) stayed on screen, or left the game on a black screen.
- **No more black bars on 16:9 games.** The screen was set up as 960×640 internally, so 16:9 games (most of them) got thin black bars at the top and bottom and the UI was slightly squashed. It now uses the real 1280×720.
- The log file is saved to the SD card once a second, so it is kept even when you close the app with HOME.

### Install / update
1. Download `Kirikiroid2-NX.nro` below and copy it to `sdmc:/switch/` (replace the old one).
2. Open the Homebrew Menu in **title-takeover mode** (hold **R** while launching a game) and start Kirikiroid2-NX. Applet mode (from the Album) does not have enough memory for most games.
3. Copy your game folder to the SD card as you would for Kirikiroid2 on Android and open `data.xp3` from the file selector.

### Known issues
- Yes/No system message boxes always pick the first button.
- Plugins not ported yet: KAGParserEx, E-mote/motion player, scriptsEx, layerExRaster, layerExMosaic, shrinkCopy and others.
- Exiting a game may show "The software was closed because an error occurred".
- Software renderer only.

Logs for bug reports are written to `sdmc:/switch/kirikiroid2/` (`k2s_boot.txt`, `k2s_log.txt`, `k2s_log.prev.txt`, `k2s_crash.txt`) — please attach them to issues.

No game data is included. Use only games you legally own. `LICENSE` and `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md` apply to the binary.

# Light is Green v1.0.6

> A clean, immersive redesign of the Cloud Library grid.

* **Clean Grid Interface (5x2)**: The game library has been redesigned to feature larger, cleaner cover art.
* **No Text Clutter**: Removed the game titles from underneath each cover for a sleeker look. The full title is still prominently displayed in the top panel when a game is focused.
* **Pure Artwork**: Dark bands and ambient padding around covers have been removed. The UI now prioritizes the native square Xbox BoxArt for a premium, edge-to-edge feel.
* **Fresh Cache**: The image cache system has been updated. It will cleanly fetch the new square covers instead of reusing the old vertical ones.
* **Full Navigation Kept**: Despite the visual overhaul, all core features—sidebar navigation, touch controls, focus memory, and pagination—remain fully intact.

packages.changelog:
Native Nintendo Switch port of Mass Effect (Xbox 360), work in progress.

### What's Changed in v0.2.1

**Please rebuild your shader package.** Packages made with the browser installer before this release missed shaders:
the values in the settings menu and the bar under its title did not draw, and two other game shaders were missing.

- **Installer:** builds every shader of your discs (31,128 of 31,128 on the Russian release with both DLC). It no longer
  skips shaders it cannot make: it retries once and otherwise stops with an error instead of writing an incomplete
  package. Fixed the browser shader translator crashing after many shaders on computers with few CPU cores.
- **Installer:** can install the full NSP straight to the console over USB from Chrome or Edge (Sphaira, Install ->
  USB); nothing is saved on the computer.
- **New companion app for macOS:** [Switch USB Installer](https://github.com/nebadasSwifty/switch-usb-installer) - drag
  an NSP onto it to install it over USB with Sphaira.
- The game itself is the same as v0.2.0.

**How to update:** open [the installer](https://nebadasSwifty.github.io/masseffect-nx/) again and build the package from
your discs, then replace the files on the SD card (at least `masseffect_shaders.mesp` and `masseffect_shaders.mesp.idx`),
or install the new full NSP.

### What's Changed in v0.2.0

**Performance**
- The scene renders at 960x544 and is upscaled to 720p with AMD FSR 1 (sharper than plain scaling at the same cost).
  Most locations now hold 30 fps; the heaviest scenes (Eden Prime after the opening cutscene, large fights) run at 20-26 fps.
- Large CPU and GPU savings in the renderer and the game code: native audio mixing and resampling (NEON), shader constants
  updated per changed vector, vertex data reused across frames, texture sign handling folded into shaders, much cheaper
  EDRAM emulation, fewer per-draw allocations, lighter kernel waits.
- Per-edition shader prewarm list: the game's pipelines are compiled in the background (from 25 s after launch), so the
  0.5-1 s stalls on the first visit of a place are gone.

**Stability**
- Fixed hangs and crashes at start: "Disc Read Error", a frozen intro / BioWare logo, a black screen. Cause: the first
  launch (no shader cache yet) compiled thousands of shaders while the game was loading, and the console ran out of
  system resources. The game now also leaves 64 MB more memory to the system.
- The screen no longer freezes on the intro when the console briefly refuses a frame.
- Long sessions no longer crash on memory fragmentation (shader cache saving, texture uploads); the shader memory use
  is about 200 MB lower.

**Image**
- Fixed missing letters in terminals, dialogues and the autosave label; characters "vanishing" on fast camera turns;
  the black start screen; Shepard rendered black.

**Controls and audio**
- Nintendo Switch button names in the game texts and the Switch layout in the decryption mini-game.
- Rumble on both Joy-Cons, scaled to the game's motor speeds.
- Experimental touch screen (handheld): drag to turn the camera, tap a dialogue option to pick it.
- Fixed a constant buzz that could replace music (XMA loops).

**Installation**
- Installable full NSP per edition (Russian and English install side by side, separate saves): the browser installer
  can build it from your own discs.
- Russian two-disc merge verified on real discs. The unused, broken `GlobalTlk_ES.xxx` of the Russian discs is now a
  short note instead of a "re-dump your discs" warning.

**Known issues**
- Pressing HOME during the first ~30 seconds after launch, while the game is loading, can freeze the console. Wait until
  the main menu.
- Rarely (about 1 launch in 10) the game can stop at the intro. Close it and start it again.
- Sysmodules and overlays use the same system memory the game's display and file access need; with many of them
  installed, the risk of the issues above grows.

### What's Changed in v0.1.3
- **Russian Edition Support*

Now based on upstream **Mega Man X Recompiled 2.2.7-alpha**.

## New
- **Boss Rush**: a new entry on the title menu. Fight the Mavericks two at a time in an endless gauntlet, with a "DEFEATED" counter and a saved high score (`mmx-boss-rush-score.dat`, next to the NRO).
- Upstream co-op camera and scene-transition fixes, netplay diagnostics and recompiler fixes.

## Fixes
- **Fixed the crash when returning to the launcher with − + L3.**
- **The boss-defeat and death flashes now light up the whole screen**, including the HUD and the widescreen side areas.
- Fixed the co-op HUD meters reading the wrong graphics in some cases.
- Diagnostic replay recording is turned off on Switch, so it no longer costs SD-card writes or performance.

The game logic matches upstream 2.2.7 frame for frame, and the picture is identical to upstream apart from the flash fix. This was verified over scripted Highway runs (as X and as Saber Zero) and a Boss Rush run.

## Install / upgrade
Replace `sdmc:/switch/MegaManX/MegaManX.nro` with the new one, or extract `MegaManX-NX.zip` to the root of your SD card. Your `config.ini`, saves and mod choices are kept.

No ROMs or game assets are included. Licensed under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, as inherited from upstream.

### Fix
- **No more immortal cars.** A badly dented car could stop taking damage: hits only count on the parts of the model near where they land, and a car dented far enough had none left there, so it could not be wasted until it reached a fix hoop. This came from the original game and hit the tougher cars most (Kool Kat, Drifter X, Sword of Justice, High Rider, EL KING, Mighty Eight, M A S H E E N). Now a car is never more dented than it is damaged (Extended's fix of the original, with its dent limits for each car), and a guard keeps those parts within reach, so every hit counts.

---

### Arreglo
- **Se acabaron los autos inmortales.** Un auto muy abollado podía dejar de recibir daño: los golpes solo cuentan en las partes del modelo cercanas a donde pegan, y un auto abollado de más ya no tenía ninguna ahí, así que no se podía destruir hasta que pasara por un aro de reparación. Venía del juego original y afectaba sobre todo a los autos más resistentes (Kool Kat, Drifter X, Sword of Justice, High Rider, EL KING, Mighty Eight, M A S H E E N). Ahora un auto nunca está más abollado que dañado (el arreglo que Extended le hizo al original, con su límite de abolladura por auto) y una protección mantiene esas partes al alcance, así que todo golpe cuenta.

packages.changelog:
# NFSMW-NX v1.0.0

First public release of NFSMW-NX: the native Nintendo Switch port of **Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2005)** (Xbox 360).

## Update (September 29, 2026)

The NROs of this release were replaced with a new build. It's still version 1.0.0.

- **Dubbed videos:** videos re-encoded by fan translations such as the Brazilian Portuguese one no longer come out
  green or with glitches. They use B-frames and the in-loop deblocking filter which the game's own videos don't.
- **Color filter:** a new setting, `nfsmw_tratamiento_visual`, makes the game's yellow tint (its "visual treatment",
  which players call the "piss filter") softer (`suave`) or turns it off (`apagado`). The default, `original`, looks
  as on the Xbox 360. It can be changed while playing from the Debug Menu (L + R + D-Pad Right), category `Graficos`.
- **Installer page:** it recognizes the Brazilian Portuguese translation which uses the Spanish PAL executable. For an
  edition it doesn't support yet, it can create `nfsmw-nx-report.txt` to send us, even from `default.xex` alone.

To update, open the installer page again, choose your game and use **Create nfsmw-nx-update.zip**. It contains only
the NRO, `nfsmw.toml` and the shader library. Copy it over your folder on the SD card: your saves are kept and the
new `nfsmw.toml` replaces yours (if you had changed a setting in it, change it again).

## How to install

Use the installer page: **https://stevensnd.github.io/nfsmw-nx-installer/**

It reads your own copy of the game in the browser and builds a package ready to copy to the SD card. The NROs
attached to this release are what the page uses: on their own they do not run, because they need the game files and
the shader library that the page builds from your disc.

## Supported editions

One NRO per edition of the game (the installer picks the right one automatically):

| File | Edition |
|---|---|
| `nfsmw-nx-pal-es.nro` | PAL - Spanish & Brazilian Portuguese (Fan Version) |
| `nfsmw-nx-pal-en.nro` | PAL - English & Russian (Fan Version) |
| `nfsmw-nx-pal-fr.nro` | PAL - French |
| `nfsmw-nx-pal-de.nro` | PAL - German |
| `nfsmw-nx-pal-it.nro` | PAL - Italian |
| `nfsmw-nx-pal-pl.nro` | PAL - Polish (Fan Version) |
| `nfsmw-nx-usa.nro` | NTSC-U |
| `nfsmw-nx-jpn.nro` | NTSC-J |
| `nfsmw-nx-kor.nro` | NTSC-K - Korean |
| `nfsmw-nx-cht.nro` | NTSC - Asia, Traditional Chinese |

## Requirements

- A Nintendo Switch that can run homebrew.
- Start `nfsmw-nx.nro` from the Homebrew Menu in title takeover mode (launch a game while holding R), or through a
  39-bit forwarder made with [Sphaira](https://github.com/NaGaa95/sphaira)

## Controls

Each Switch button acts as the Xbox 360 button with the same letter: **A** accepts and **B** goes back, as in other
Switch games, also in the Debug Menu. To use the face buttons by position instead, as on an Xbox pad (B acts as A,
A as B, Y as X and X as Y), set `input_xbox_layout = true` in `nfsmw.toml`.

## Resolution

Automatic by default: **1280x720** in handheld mode and **1920x1080** docked, chosen when the game starts (after
docking or undocking, restart the game to switch). To use one resolution in both modes, set
`nfsmw_resolucion_interna` to `1280x720` or `1920x1080` in `nfsmw.toml`. If the frame rate is too low docked, use
`1280x720`.

## Notes

- The Debug Menu (L + R + Right) and the log files are in Spanish in this version.
- The first race after installing or updating compiles the graphics pipelines it has not seen yet, so it can stutter
  for a few seconds. They are saved on the SD card and later sessions start smoothly.
- Performance, overclocking and all the settings are explained in the README.
- Source code and documentation: this repository. The code of these NROs is the `main` branch as of September 29,
  2026. The licenses of the NRO and its libraries are in `LICENSE` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

packages.changelog:
Land 1, closer to the original. Much of this release comes from the [bw1-decomp](https://github.com/openblack/bw1-decomp) project's decompilation of the original game, and from checking against the original running under Wine.

### What's new

- **Villagers live their days as in the original:** they work, rest, get hungry and eat from the village store, housewives fetch food home for dinner, and they sleep at night. Farmers sow and harvest; builders fetch wood and build. They walk at the original's pace.
- **The opening's dance** around the statue, to the original's own choreography.
- **Reward chests:** the original's treasure chest falls from the sky, and its lid swings open with the original's sounds when clicked, giving food, wood or a miracle.
- **Your creature moves like the original's:** animations at their own speeds, posed with the original's maths, easing between standing and walking, feet kept to the ground.
- **The hand:** the original's poses and animation; it holds things between thumb and forefinger, closing round them by their size, and its fingers trail as it moves.
- **Throwing:** things fly as in the original: rocks far and straight, trees, people and miracles slowing in the air.
- **Miracle spheres** as in the original: the animated glassy bubble with the miracle's icon turning upright inside, resting on its dispenser, and the original's particle effects for the water and fire spheres.
- **ZL** at the Temple's door goes in. Normal speed is paced to match the original.

### Installing

1. Put `openblack.nro` at `sdmc:/switch/openblack/openblack.nro` (replace the old one to update).
2. Copy the `Data`, `Audio` and `Scripts` folders from **your own** Black & White PC installation into `sdmc:/switch/openblack/game/`. This release contains no game data.
3. Launch with full memory: hold **R** while starting any game to open the Homebrew Menu, then choose openblack.

Needs Atmosphère and the Homebrew Menu. Controls, what works and known limitations are in the [README](https://github.com/gitgarage/openblack/blob/switch-port/README.md).

### Known limitations

Only Land 1 for now; miracles are cast from spheres, not gestures; the heal, lightning, shield and teleport spheres don't show their particle effects yet; saving uses two save points on the D-pad.

Bug reports are welcome; please attach `sdmc:/switch/openblack/openblack.log`.

---

openPREY: Prey (2006) running natively on the Nintendo Switch as homebrew. A port of OpenPrey (id Tech 4); requires your own PC copy of the game.

packages.changelog:
First public release of **openPREY**, a homebrew port of Prey (2006) for the Nintendo Switch, built on [OpenPrey](https://github.com/themuffinator/OpenPrey).

> **You need your own copy of Prey (2006) for PC.** No game data is included.

## Installation

1. Extract `openPREY-switch-0.1.0.zip` to the **root of the SD card**. This creates `switch/openprey/`.
2. Copy **every `.pk4` file** from the `base` folder of your Prey installation into `switch/openprey/base/`.
3. Hold **R** while starting any installed game (title override) and pick **openPREY** in the Homebrew Menu. It does not run from the Album.

The first visit to each map takes a few minutes while its texture cache is built; later loads are much faster. Full instructions, controls and tips are in the [README](https://github.com/hazevauks/openPREYswitch#readme).

## Highlights

- Prey's single-player campaign from your own PC files, with saving and loading.
- A 30 fps frame lock and dynamic resolution, up to 1280×720.
- Controls in the style of modern console shooters, optional gyro aiming, touch in menus and the system keyboard.
- A settings menu on the **−** button: FPS counter, frame lock, shadows, dynamic resolution, GPU clock profile, gyro, look speed, subtitles and noclip.
- Prey's own collision and monster navigation (AAS) data, loaded as shipped.
- Logs, crash reports and death reports on the SD card, ready for bug reports.

## Tested

Played on hardware from the start of the campaign, through the Land of the Ancients, up to the Leech Gun in the feeding tower, mostly in handheld mode with the CPU at 1224 MHz. With shadows off, the opening maps hold 30 fps, dipping to about 25 in the busiest moments. Later chapters have not been tested yet.

## Known issues

- **No Deathwalk.** When Tommy dies he does not go to the Deathwalk; the game continues from the last save.
- **Long first loads** of each map while its texture cache is built.
- **Some busy areas drop below 30 fps.** Performance is the focus of the next updates.
- **`vid_restart` leaves the screen black.** Restart the game instead.
- **No multiplayer.** Docked mode has had less testing than handheld.

## Reporting bugs

Open an [issue](https://github.com/hazevauks/openPREYswitch/issues) with `switch/openprey/basepr/logs/openprey.log` (plus `openprey-previous.log` and `switch/openprey/openprey_crash.txt` when they exist), and say where in the game it happened.

## Oracles NX 1.0

First release of Oracles NX, a native Nintendo Switch port of **Oracle of Ages** and **Oracle of Seasons**, built on [oracles-decomp](https://github.com/kirby-letsgo/oracles-decomp) by kirby-letsgo.

The games run as native C code: no CPU emulator and no ROM code.

### Features
- Both games in one app, with a launcher showing each game's save files
- Save states (4 slots with thumbnails) and a Resume state on quit
- Screen filters (sharp, scanlines, LCD grid, CRT) and widescreen 16:9 mode
- Fully remappable controls and fast-forward (hold ZR)
- Full screen in handheld (720p) and docked (1080p)

### Installation
1. Copy `oracles.nro` to `sdmc:/switch/oracles/`
2. Copy your own **USA / Australia** ROMs (`.gbc`, `.zip` or `.gz`) to `sdmc:/switch/oracles/roms/`
3. Launch Oracles NX from the Homebrew Menu. The ROMs are installed on first launch.

Only the USA / Australia versions are supported (checked by SHA1). See the README for the hashes.

### Default controls
A / B: A / B · +: Start · −: Select · R: pause menu · ZR (hold): fast-forward

> **No game files are included.** You need your own ROMs. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo or Capcom.

### Credits
All the real work on the game reimplementation is by **kirby-letsgo** ([oracles-decomp](https://github.com/kirby-letsgo/oracles-decomp)), based on the [oracles-disasm](https://github.com/Drenn1/oracles-disasm) community disassembly. Switch port by **Toniisound**.

## What's new in 1.6.4 (compared to 1.6.3)

**In short:** eliminated Horizon OS FS hangs and Atmosphère NCM panics during large game installs; preserved file selection access on completed downloads for grabbing extra DLCs, patches, and translations; dynamic NRO relocation and robust in-app updating; reliable Switch port deployment; fixed catalog sorting and repack classification.

### Installation & Storage Stability (Critical)

- **Upfront NCM placeholder allocation (`a69240e`):** reverted dynamic 256 MiB placeholder chunk resizing (`ncmContentStorageSetPlaceHolderSize`) back to standard upfront full-size placeholder creation (`ncmContentStorageCreatePlaceHolder`). On FAT32 SD cards, mid-stream placeholder resizing caused heavy SDMMC bus lockups, deadlocking Horizon OS FS and triggering an unrecoverable `std::abort()` panic in Atmosphère's NCM sysmodule (`0100000000000002`). This also resolves issues with 4GB+ NCA split files (`CreateOption_BigFile`).
- **Filesystem directory creation fix (`b45895d`):** normalized `mkdirs` across install and download pipelines to strip the device mount prefix (`sdmc:/`) and trailing slashes, preventing failed `mkdir` calls under libnx.

### Downloads & File Management

- **File selection for existing & completed tasks (`ee204d3`):** kept the "Select files" button accessible on the game detail card even when a release is already active or finished, replacing redundant "View download" links.
- **Incremental file downloads:** opening file selection on an existing task pre-populates previous choices, allowing users to effortlessly select and download additional DLCs, voiceovers, or community translations without deleting existing completed downloads.
- **Fast-path metainfo reuse:** opening file selection immediately reads cached metainfo without waiting for redundant network re-announces.

### In-App Updater & Path Relocation

- **Dynamic NRO relocation (`b66d441`):** resolved the active executable path from `argv[0]`, ensuring smooth in-app updates even if the NRO binary was renamed or placed in non-standard SD card locations.
- **Duplicate NRO cleanup & sync:** cleanly updates the running binary, synchronizing duplicates and removing orphaned intermediate files on the SD card.
- **In-app update notifications restored:** restored reliable update checking in Settings and accurate update prompt banners.

### Ports & Deployments

- **Direct Switch port deployment (`b45895d`):** enabled starting PortInstall tasks with manual approval from `SwitchDeployPreviewActivity` directly on the console without requiring web panel rule triggers.
- **Deployment UX improvements:** prevented duplicate actions during in-flight port operations and surfaced detailed error messages on deployment failures.

### Catalog & Classification

- **Repack & full game classification (`caf624a`):** classified full game repacks and multi-content bundles under the Games tab rather than misidentifying them as standalone updates.
- **MIG Switch & media routing:** routed MIG Switch (.xci/.xcz) and media assets to the Ports / Archives section with sanitized package types.
- **Catalog sorting regression fix (`5da20cf`):** restored proper release date and name sorting across catalog views.
- **Updated catalog snapshot:** refreshed bundled offline catalog data.

# PPSSPP Switch Version 0.6.5

Nintendo Switch community release based on PPSSPP v1.20.4.

## Highlights

- Added hardware-tested ARM64 JIT cache-pointer preservation fixes.
- Corrected the tested ARM64 IR/JIT cache-pointer crash path.
- Added parallel software depth rasterization using safe, non-overlapping worker tiles.
- Added Nintendo Switch process-core detection for worker scheduling.
- Corrected affected texture and CLUT memory reads.
- Fixed video swizzle-buffer initialization and ownership.
- Corrected negative render-target offsets in the OpenGL ES path.
- Fixed SDL trigger mapping and right-stick diagonal threshold behavior.
- Improved native Switch keyboard and multilingual input support.
- Added fallback fonts for CJK, Arabic, Hebrew, Thai and Lao.
- Retains the validated FFmpeg 57 video and 48 kHz audio fixes from Version 0.6.0.

## Installation

1. Download `PPSSPP-Switch-0.6.5.zip`.
2. Extract the ZIP to the root of the Nintendo Switch SD card.
3. Confirm that the application is installed at:

   `SD:/switch/ppsspp/PPSSPP.nro`

4. Fully close and reopen the Homebrew Menu after replacing an older version so its icon and metadata refresh.

## Recommended Configuration

- CPU core: JIT
- Graphics backend: OpenGL ES

Version 0.6.5 includes the tested ARM64 IR/JIT correction, but regular JIT remains recommended for the widest compatibility. Vulkan is not supported.

## Package Identity

- Application: PPSSPP
- Author metadata: PPSSPP Team
- Version: 0.6.5
- Runtime directory: `/switch/ppsspp/`
- ZIP SHA-256: `78ae639f28e371260f52dccb05dfd820bc81c8086457a251674e0185922c6297`

Hey, as promised in the last update - I sat down and rewrote the UI from scratch. This time, we're using Model-View architecture to the best of my ability. It works, it is less glitchy - but most importantly - bug fixes are easier now than ever. I have been testing it for a while and almost everything works out of the box and I have experienced zero crashing anywhere - if you do, please do let me know on either GBATemp or Discord. I'll try my best to release an update as soon as possible. 

## Changelog:
** This update touches shaders. You will have crashes if you don't clear your shader cache after this update. **
- Rewrote the UI from scratch. It uses GPU Composition now, and does not bully the CPU like it did on our previous UI. In idle mode, it uses basically zero power, instead of previously where it would drain close to 0.4W of power in idle. This does not affect power draw in-game since UI is not rendered in-game. 
- Added bunch of options to screen layout editor: per-screen rotation, layering, per-game layout editor, and more.
- Added a UI for enabling and disabling Mods. This is NOT tested and uses the same backend as Azahar so it should technically work. Please report if it isn't working. 
- Added box art and game description scraping from [GameTDB](https://www.gametdb.com/3DS). Game descriptions are scrapped and added in the build by default, you can download the box arts if needed.
- Fixed a critical issue where it would take 3-4 extra seconds to boot up a game for no reason. The game boots after compiling pipelines is super fast now.
- Separated save files, ROMs folder, 
- Upstreamed to latest Azahar build as of 18/08/2026. 
- Updated NVK to latest 26.2.0.
- Added option to go back to library from in-game settings.
- Rewrote a few functions for shader compilation via dynarmic and some in NXVK. Reduces stutters slightly after the first huge ones.
- Completely rewrote the UI input handler. It now supports multi-inputs and all UI controls are now completely remappable.
- Added many Quality of Life updates and small patches that I genuinely wanted to use for myself. 

##

I will release the source code for the previous updates in a week or two. I had surgery a few days ago due to a freak accident so I have been unable to sit on PC for long periods of time. P.S. If you are going to use my code, even if rewriting it, please at least give proper attributions.

## Sonic 4: Episode II NX v0.2

This release adds full FMV playback support for the opening movie and in-game cutscenes.

### Added

- Added FFmpeg-based MP4 playback.
- Added support for the game's MPEG-4/H.264 video and AAC audio streams.
- Added playback for all in-game cutscenes and localized staff-roll videos.
- Added support for the SEGA opening movie (`sega_720.mp4`).
- Added A, B, and Plus button controls for skipping videos.
- Added FMV performance and audio diagnostics to `debug.log`.

### Fixed

- Fixed cutscenes being immediately bypassed because `VideoIsPlaying()` always returned false.
- Fixed extremely slow playback caused by an audio-clock/demux deadlock.
- Fixed cutscene audio by mixing FMV PCM into the game's existing SDL audio device.
- Fixed legacy packed MPEG-4 videos playing twice after reaching their intended ending.
- Fixed excessive `VideoIsPlaying` polling logs causing heavy SD-card I/O.
- Fixed unnecessary OpenGL texture reallocation on every video frame.
- Fixed video requests being processed from a thread without the active EGL context.

### Installation note

from the base APK and copy it to:

The regular cutscene MP4 files must remain inside:

`sdmc:/switch/s4ep2/assets/`

### Build requirements

Building from source now additionally requires:

- `switch-ffmpeg`

### Notes

packages.changelog:
The installer page installs this version: https://chanseyisthebest.github.io/sa2-nx-installer/

To update by hand instead, replace `sa2.nro` in `switch/sa2-nx/` on the SD card with the one below. The game files,
the shader package and your `sa2.toml` stay as they are. Logging and the profiler are off, as in every release.

## What it changes against 1.0.1

- **Long sessions:** after a few hours of play, earlier versions could show black textures and missing level
  geometry, objects and enemies until the game was closed and opened again. The renderer has 4,096 slots for
  textures, and its texture cache only released textures by the size of their pixel data. Sonic Adventure 2's
  textures are so small that the slots ran out first, and every texture first seen after that was drawn black or
  not at all. The cache now also releases the textures unused for the longest when the slots run low
  (`sa2_native_texture_slots_evict`).
- **Render-target copies:** the renderer kept a copy of every render-target texture (mostly shadow maps) for the
  whole session. Copies the game no longer uses are now released (`sa2_native_resolved_retire_idle`, from the 1.0.2
  pre-release).

Everything in 1.0.1 is still there: the faster CPU code and the Chao garden shadow fix.

**If the game crashes**, please send `switch/sa2-nx/logs/rex/rex_crash.log` from the SD card. It is written even
with logging off, and it says what went wrong; the console's own crash report does not.

Details: [docs/enhancements.md](https://github.com/ChanseyIsTheBest/sa2-nx/blob/main/docs/enhancements.md). Setting
either key to `false` in `sa2.toml` gives the old behaviour.

`sa2.nro` SHA-256: `d8db93683069107d79d22c3bded0a18ed0f880469c1faab147490d4c9f67154d`

packages.changelog:
Silent Hill 2 (Director's Cut / Restless Dreams) on the Switch: the PC game's executable recompiled to native ARM64, no emulator, with support for the Silent Hill 2: Enhanced Edition packs.

**What's changed in v1.01**

- The game runs at its original 30 fps: the experimental 60 fps mode (`fps=60`) was removed.
- Sharper by default: 1920x1080, drawn at 720p handheld and 1080p docked (`resolution`, `handheld` and `docked` in `sh2e.ini`). If your `sh2e.ini` sets `resolution=1280x720`, `handheld=480` or `docked=720`, remove those lines to get the new defaults.
- Russian, Japanese and other non-Latin text ([#14](https://github.com/cutarev/sh2-nx/issues/14)): the Enhanced Edition's high resolution font (`sh2e/font`) is used now, and translations made for the Enhanced Edition load from a `lang` folder next to the NRO.

**Features**

- **Native code**: every function of `sh2pc.exe` runs as ARM64 code; no emulator, no Wine.
- **Widescreen**: 16:9, drawn at 720p handheld and 1080p docked, or the original 4:3 (ThirteenAG's WidescreenFix, ported).
- **Enhanced Edition packs**: HD textures and maps, the EE title and save screens, the restored music, voices and sound effects, EE menus and fonts, and the FMV pack's 1080p60 movies with their subtitles (`movie=1`).
- **Enhanced Edition fixes**: search camera on the right stick, movement on the d-pad, pause menu fix, vibration fixes.
- **Controller**: SH2EE's button layout with Nintendo's A/B, HD rumble following the in-game Vibration option.
- **Saving and loading**, movies with synced audio, every menu.
- **Shader cache**: shaders are compiled once and kept on the SD card, so areas only stutter the first time.
- Also builds for Linux (x86-64), which is where most of the debugging happens.

**Install**

1. On your PC, install Silent Hill 2 and run the Enhanced Edition setup with at least the Enhanced Executable, Essential Files, Image Enhancement Pack and Audio Enhancement Pack (plus the FMV Enhancement Pack for the HD movies). The port is built for that `sh2pc.exe` (5,685,248 bytes, SHA-1 `3201a5e1029f3ae3b77770255dcbe10360b3cd09`).
2. Put `sh2-nx.nro` in `/switch/sh2-nx/` on the SD card, together with `sh2pc.exe`, `data/` and `sh2e/` from your PC install, and an `sh2e.ini` ([example](https://github.com/cutarev/sh2-nx/blob/main/docs/sh2e.ini.example)). Updating from an older version: replace the NRO; for the HD movies also copy `sh2e/movie` and set `movie=1` in your `sh2e.ini`.
3. Launch it from the homebrew menu in title takeover mode (hold R while starting an installed game), not from the album.

Full instructions, controls and settings: see the [README](https://github.com/cutarev/sh2-nx#how-to-install). No game files are included.

# Sonic Advance 2 NX v0.3

This update adds an optional retry shortcut to normal stages and Special Stages.

## What's new

- Added a retry option after completing a normal stage.
- Added retry support on the Game Over and Time Over screens.
- Added retry support after both successful and failed Special Stages.
- Added an on-screen retry prompt using X by default.
- Added a configurable `retry` binding with support for any button accepted by `config.ini`.
- Added `retry = NONE` support for players who prefer the original automatic flow.
- Preserved cleared-stage progress before replaying a completed normal stage.
- Preserved Special Stage score and Chaos Emerald rewards before replaying a successful attempt.

## Controls and configuration

The default retry button is X. Existing v0.2 configuration files do not need to be replaced; retry still defaults to X when the entry is absent.

To choose another button, close the game and add or edit this entry in:

```text
sdmc:/switch/sonic_advance_2/config.ini
```

Example:

```ini
[controls]
retry = ZR
```

To disable the retry prompt and retain the original result timing:

```ini
[controls]
retry = NONE
```

On normal Stage Clear screens, the prompt appears after score counting finishes. On Special Stage results, A continues and the configured retry button immediately starts the same Special Stage again.

## Updating from v0.2

Replace the old NRO with `sonic_advance2_nx_v0.3.nro`. Existing save data and `config.ini` files are preserved.

The port still requires a clean USA Sonic Advance 2 ROM at:

```text
sdmc:/switch/sonic_advance_2/sa2.gba
```

Expected ROM SHA-1:

```text
7bcd6a07af7c894746fa28073fe0c0e34408022d
```

## Known issues

- Some title-screen graphics and text can be offset or clipped.
- Parts of the character-selection screen can be misaligned.
- The world map / stage-selection screen can contain shifted elements.
- Some in-engine or illustrated story cutscenes can show offsets, clipping or incorrectly placed layers.
- Multiplayer and Tiny Chao Garden are not supported.

## Download verification

SHA-256 (`sonic_advance2_nx_v0.3.nro`):

```text
943af1044dbc04eaa5956d0fec0c6fb55d433dcc3c63f0c6f40feb1295046cff
```

This is an unofficial fan-made port. No ROM is included; users must provide their own legally obtained copy.

# Sonic R NX v0.1.0

Initial Nintendo Switch release of **Sonic R NX**, an unofficial Switch port of the open-source [[Sonic R reimplementation](https://github.com/jnmartin84/sonic-r)](https://github.com/jnmartin84/sonic-r) by jnmartin84.

This first release focuses on stability, native Switch support, and cross-platform multiplayer.

## Features

* Native Nintendo Switch homebrew build
* Stable **30 FPS** gameplay
* Full-screen 16:9 presentation
* Switch-specific GLES rendering compatibility layer
* Nintendo Switch controller support
* Switch-friendly network lobby controls
* Nintendo Switch software keyboard support
* Automatic save and ghost directory creation
* LAN multiplayer
* **PC ↔ Nintendo Switch cross-play**
* Automatic LAN host discovery
* Direct IP connection support
* Experimental internet play by connecting the Switch directly to a reachable PC host
* Custom Homebrew Menu icon

## Network Controls

* **L** — Host / Start Race
* **R** — Join / Search
* **Y** — LAN Mode
* **D-Pad Left / Right** — Change Character
* **D-Pad Up / Down** — Change Track
* **ZR** — Change Game Mode
* **Minus (-)** — Open Network Keyboard
* **Plus (+)** — Direct IP Join
* **A** — Confirm / Send
* **B** — Back

## Online Play

Full native matchmaking is not yet available on the Nintendo Switch version.

However, the Switch can connect directly to a PC host using its IP address, including over the internet if the PC host is reachable on UDP port **7847**.

Because of this, **PC ↔ Switch internet cross-play is partially supported**, although the Switch currently cannot independently sign into the upstream matchmaking service.

## Installation

Copy:

```text
sonicr.nro
```

to:

```text
sdmc:/switch/sonic-r/
```

You must provide your own legally owned Sonic R game data.

See the repository README for the required folder structure and setup instructions.

## Notes

* This release intentionally uses the original **30 Hz gameplay simulation** for stability.
* Experimental 60 FPS support was tested during development but is not included in this release.
* PC and Switch players should use compatible builds and matching game data for multiplayer.
* No original Sonic R assets are included.

## Credits

Huge thanks to **jnmartin84** for the Sonic R reimplementation that made this port possible.

Nintendo Switch port by **Bora Eskicioğlu**.

---

This is an early release, so bug reports and testing feedback are welcome.

# Sonic the Fighters NX v0.8.3

Sonic the Fighters comes to Nintendo Switch through **m2-hle2**, with Switch-specific rendering and audio, widescreen support, native controls, and the original arcade game flow.

## Highlights

- **External ROM loading:** supply your own `sfight.zip` on the SD card. No game ROM is included or embedded in the NRO.
- **Original arcade menus:** the original title screen and character selection are preserved.
- **In-game pause:** press Minus (−) to pause a match and press it again to resume, with the game timer and audio paused together.
- **ZR Hyper shortcut:** activate the original Hyper command with one button; normal activation conditions and barrier cost still apply.
- **Earlier Super Sonic access:** play as Sonic, collect seven Chaos Emeralds, and activate Hyper from stage 8 onward. The no-loss, no-continue, and Metal Sonic second-round restrictions are removed.
- **Rebalanced defense:** Super Sonic takes one quarter of incoming damage, rounded up to at least 1 for positive hits. He can still be knocked out.
- **Widescreen and rendering work:** includes the prior Switch-focused renderer, texture-upload, loading, and audio improvements.
- **ROM-free builds and releases:** the build and release scripts reject embedded RomFS and do not require a game ROM to compile.

## Installation

Extract the release ZIP to the root of your SD card, then add your own compatible ROM:

| File | Required SD-card path |
|---|---|
| Application | `SD:/switch/sonic_fighters_nx/sonic_fighters_nx.nro` |
| Your ROM | `SD:/switch/sonic_fighters_nx/sfight.zip` |

Keep `sfight.zip` zipped and named exactly as shown. Launch the application from the Homebrew Menu in application mode (title takeover).

**Upgrading from an embedded-ROM build?** Replace the older NRO and provide `sfight.zip` separately. Missing, empty, or invalid archives display an explanatory error; B or Plus (+) exits the error screen.

## Controls

| Action | Input |
|---|---|
| Move | Left stick / D-pad |
| Punch | B |
| Kick | A |
| Guard | Y |
| Hyper Mode | ZR |
| Start | Plus (+) |
| Pause / Resume | Minus (−), during gameplay |
| Exit | ZL + ZR + Plus (+) |

## Notes

- The external-ROM version has been reported working on real Switch hardware by the port maintainer.
- This release makes no new fixed-FPS or overclock claim.
- Game ROMs must be supplied by the user and are not distributed with the project.

Thanks to **[biggestsonicfan and the m2-hle2 contributors](https://github.com/biggestsonicfan/m2-hle2)**, devkitPro/libnx, Mesa/Nouveau, sokol, and miniz. Nintendo Switch port by **[Bora Eskicioğlu / BESK](https://github.com/boraeskicioglu)**.

### **Release v1.0.0**

First release of the Sonic Triple Trouble 16-Bit wrapper for the Nintendo Switch. The game is fully playable from start to finish at a locked 60 FPS.

**What Works**

1. **Fully Playable:** The game can be completed from start to finish without crashes.
2. **Locked 60 FPS**: Native ARM64 execution with no emulation layer. The GMS2 runner runs directly on Switch hardware at full clock speed.
3. **Full Controller Support:** All physical buttons are mapped — A, B, X, Y, D-Pad (all 4 directions), both analog sticks, +, −, L, R, ZL, ZR. D-Pad support was implemented via reverse-engineered GameMaker's internal Hat event system (onGPNativeHat) rather than raw key codes.
4. **Analog Stick:** Both sticks work correctly with a deadzone filter and drift prevention. Startup centering is handled to eliminate the self-locking diagonal drift issue common in GMS2 ports.
5. **Full Audio:** Stereo audio using a custom OpenSL ES → SDL2 software mixer shim with full sound effects and background music.
6. **Save Data:** Game progress and settings persist correctly. Saves are flushed safely on exit and when the application is backgrounded.
7. **Performance:** Optimized with -O3 -ffast-math, extended CPU boost window for asset loading, and a larger SDL2 audio buffer to minimize callback overhead and frame time spikes.

**Known Issues**

None known at this time. Please open an issue if you encounter anything unexpected.

## SuperModel NX 1.4.0

### Game fixes
- **The Lost World**: no longer stays on a black screen after the boot text with the recompiler on, and now runs at full speed (60 fps).
- **The Lost World**: the gun calibration is fixed automatically in its NVRAM, so no manual calibration is needed (the original file is kept as `.nv.bak`).
- **The Lost World / Ocean Hunter / LA Machineguns**: analog gun controls fixed. The crosshair no longer sticks to the top-left corner; aim with the left stick, shoot with ZR or A.
- **Ocean Hunter**: boots again.
- **Daytona USA 2 Power Edition**: fixed a slowdown to ~3 fps in 3D scenes.

### Recompiler (JIT) improvements
- Guest CPU time per frame is now exact, as with the interpreter. Games that time their frames with the CPU timer no longer drift or lock up.
- Interrupts are handled like the interpreter: right after the store that raises them, and after `mtmsr`/`mtspr`.
- `blr`/`bctr` jump straight to already-compiled code. Busy-wait loops are much cheaper.
- Writing data next to code no longer throws away all compiled code; only writes to actual code do.
- SCSI and Real3D DMA transfers that overwrite code now invalidate the compiled code correctly.

### From official Supermodel
- 3D: Step 2.x games (Harley-Davidson, Ski Champ, Emergency Call Ambulance, Ocean Hunter) no longer follow junk links that could loop or draw objects twice; plus fog, level-of-detail and memory bounds fixes.
- Drive board: servo registers, command queue and four force feedback effects per axis (better vibration in racing games).
- Virtua Striker 2 '98: corrected ROM CRC.

### Other
- The settings menu no longer deletes the per-game sections of `Supermodel.ini` when saving.
- New `Supermodel.ini` options for troubleshooting: `JitChainIndirect`, `JitInlineDEC`, `JitInterpret` and `LogCpuWait`.
- The performance report in `Supermodel.log` now also shows I/O reads, raised IRQs, exceptions, and JIT compiles and cache flushes per frame.
