packages.changelog:
A small fix release on top of v0.7.13:

- **Streaming no longer stops for good after a homebrew app.** After you closed some homebrew apps (Sphaira, for example), the next game could fail to stream, with no picture or the viewer stuck on "starting the stream", until you rebooted. The app's graphics memory left a gap that Switch Frame Tap's own buffers then fell into, and the video engine can't use that address. Switch Frame Tap now fills that gap before it sets up a stream.
- **Windows viewer: sharp on scaled displays.** At 125-300 % scaling (a 4K TV, for example), Windows drew the viewer at 100 % and stretched it, so the picture and text looked soft. The window still opens at the same size on screen.
- **Fullscreen on a screen that isn't 16:9** (a TV set to 4096x2160, for example) now shows a note suggesting a 16:9 mode, so you get no side bars.
- The overlay's and the app's version now show correctly in the Tesla / Ultrahand menu (they said 0.7.11).

Nothing else changed: the Switch side is v0.7.13 plus this fix.

Want the HOME menu on the stream too? That's in [v0.7.14-beta1](https://github.com/TomasUribe/switch-frame-tap/releases/tag/v0.7.14-beta1) (opt-in).

**Installing:** unzip `switch-frame-tap-0.7.13.1-switch.zip` over the SD card root and reboot (settings are kept), and update the viewer.

## What's new

- **Smooth 60 fps videos.** YouTube videos at 60 fps (sent with the AirPlay button) now run on a steady clock. On a Switch OLED, frames skipped dropped from 10–24% to 0–0.3% at both 720p and 1080p.
- **Resolution is 1080p by default.** If the picture stutters on a weak Wi-Fi, choose 1280 × 720 in Settings (−). The Automatic option from 1.1.0 (720p handheld, 1080p docked) is gone, and if you had it selected you now get 1080p. A size you set yourself in `config.ini` is kept.
- **Simpler stats overlay** (X button). It shows only the share of frames shown over the last few seconds, for example "Frames shown: 99.6%", with no growing frame count.
- **Debug logs are complete.** With `debug_log = true`, the copies in `/config/SwitchAirCast/logs/` now start with the first lines of each run and no longer lose lines while YouTube sends its playlists.

## Upgrading

Replace `/switch/SwitchAirCast.nro` with the new file. Your settings are kept.

## Install

1. Download `SwitchAirCast.nro` below and copy it to `/switch/` on your SD card. (Or download the zip and extract it to the root of the SD card.)
2. Open the Homebrew Menu **through a game** (hold **R** while starting any game) and start SwitchAirCast.
3. On your iPhone, iPad or Mac (same Wi-Fi network): Control Center → **Screen Mirroring** → choose your Switch.

See the [README](https://github.com/depende3000/SwitchAirCast#readme) for all buttons, settings and troubleshooting.

## Reporting a problem

Open an issue and attach `log.txt` and `log-previous.txt` from `/config/SwitchAirCast/` on the SD card, plus the newest file in `/atmosphere/crash_reports/` if the app crashed. With `debug_log = true` the log is much more detailed, and the last 10 runs are kept in `/config/SwitchAirCast/logs/`.

# SwitchNOW 1.2.0 - Integration and Experience Update

Welcome to a major feature and reliability update for **SwitchNOW**, the native GeForce NOW homebrew client for Nintendo Switch.

- **Free Tier Ads Support:** Added full support for mandatory NVIDIA video advertisements on the GeForce NOW Free tier.
- **Persistent Authentication:** Significantly improved long-term NVIDIA authentication by utilizing `client_token`.
- **TLS Fixes:** Fixed authentication issues affecting some Switch consoles and older `libnx` certificate stores.
- **1080p Docked Mode:** Substantially improved interface scaling and navigation when the console is docked.
- **Safer Search:** Improved library and catalog search with reliable asynchronous result handling.
- **Expanded Localization:** Added deeper translations across session startup, queue, and advertisement states.
- **Under the Hood:** Multiple UI, focus, shortcut, and stability fixes throughout the application.

## HOME Menu Game Shortcuts

SwitchNOW can now create a dedicated HOME Menu shortcut for any individual GeForce NOW game.

To use this feature, open a game's details page and press the new `+` action button.

**Each shortcut:**
- Uses the game's title and automatically generates square artwork.
- Appears directly alongside your native games on the Nintendo Switch HOME Menu.
- Opens SwitchNOW and automatically launches the selected game.
- Preserves your chosen storefront (e.g. Steam, Epic) when multiple versions are available.
- Securely piggybacks on your existing SwitchNOW authentication without storing credentials inside the shortcut itself.

*Note: A standard launcher NRO and manifest are also created under `sdmc:/switch/SwitchNOW Shortcuts/`.*

> [!IMPORTANT]
> HOME Menu shortcut installation requires SwitchNOW to be running in **Application mode** (Hold `R` while launching an installed game).

## Built-in Updates

SwitchNOW can now check for new releases directly from the Settings menu. Updates are securely downloaded only from the official SwitchNOW GitHub repository.

The updater uses a separate, minimal helper application to ensure maximum safety:
- **Integrity Checks:** Verifies the download using SHA-256 before proceeding.
- **Safe Backups:** Automatically backs up your existing SwitchNOW installation.
- **Fail-safes:** Automatically rolls back if the installation fails.
- **Consistent Paths:** Maintains a stable `sdmc:/switch/SwitchNOW/SwitchNOW.nro` application path.

*Note: Update checks are strictly manual — SwitchNOW does not automatically ping for updates or display annoying update prompts at startup.*

SwitchNOW now fully supports NVIDIA's mandatory advertisement flow for Free-tier sessions.

1. SwitchNOW enters a dedicated advertisement stage.

- **Pause menu over a black or old picture** ([#20](https://github.com/centollOS/SwitchWaker/issues/20)): with "Depth of field" turned off, the pause menu opened over a black screen or a frame from earlier. Thanks to gptnooui for the report.
- **Letter sorting game in the Rito post office** ([#19](https://github.com/centollOS/SwitchWaker/issues/19)): a letter could show another letter's picture. Thanks to MrGroovee for the report.

## Install / update

Pick the download for your disc:

| Your disc | Download | Disc image |
|---|---|---|
| USA (`GZLE01`, revision 0) | `SwitchWaker-v0.5.0-switch.zip` | `sdmc:/switch/switchwaker/GZLE01.iso` |
| Europe (`GZLP01`, revision 0) | `SwitchWaker-v0.5.0-switch-eur.zip` | `sdmc:/switch/switchwaker/GZLP01.iso` |

- **Updating from 0.4.x:** copy the zip's `switch` folder over the old one. Your disc, saves, settings and the HOME-screen icon stay as they are.
- **New install:** copy the zip's `switch` folder to the root of the SD card and put your disc image (uncompressed `.iso`) at the path above. Details: **[INSTALL.md](https://github.com/centollOS/SwitchWaker/blob/v0.5.0/INSTALL.md)**.
- One region per SD card: both downloads install `sdmc:/switch/switchwaker/switchwaker.nro`.

## Known issues

- "Instant text" does not speed up the text of some cutscenes (for example the arrival on Outset Island).
- The disc's videos (the title screen's attract video and the ending video) do not play yet.
- Docked at 60 fps the frame rate can still drop to 30 in heavy scenes.

Credits, licenses and how AI was used: see the README.

# Alek’s Ultimate NX Edition — Public Beta 2

A packaging fix for Beta 1. The Beta 1 ZIP did not include the Luau runtime folder, so every Luau script mod (for example **Linkle Mod**) failed with:

> Mod requires a service that is unavailable (missing: dev.twilitrealm.luau)

## What changed

- Added `switch/dusklight/mods/luau_runtime/`. Luau support is built into `dusklight.nro`, but the mod loader only provides the `dev.twilitrealm.luau` service when this folder is on the SD card.
- `dusklight.nro`, `randomizer.dusk` and `twilit_essentials.dusk` are byte-for-byte identical to Beta 1.

## Installing or updating

1. Close the game and back up the complete `sdmc:/switch/dusklight/` folder. It contains your saves, settings, mods and mod data.
2. Extract `Alek-Ultimate-NX-v1.0.0-beta.2.zip` to the root of your SD card.
3. If you are new: put a dump of your own Twilight Princess disc (.iso, .gcm, .rvz, .wia or .gcz) in `sdmc:/switch/dusklight/` or `sdmc:/switch/dusklight/discs/`.
4. Luau support, Randomizer and Twilit Essentials are native mods. Native mods start in Dry Run. To enable them, select **Settings → Aleks → Diagnostics → Native Mods: Loader Mode → Execute**, then restart the game.

Already on Beta 1? You only need the new `luau_runtime` folder, but extracting the whole ZIP is also safe.

No copyrighted game data is included.

## Verification

ZIP SHA-256:

`d70c3b49b4d5ed4f3066f3755c68e7968e02950650f0c03958c2d17a4930f533`

The NRO is the same one as in Beta 1, built from commit `5bb1da87d3`. Everything else in the Beta 1 release notes still applies, including the known mod issues.

This is an independent fan fork and is not affiliated with Twilit Realm or Nintendo. Full credits and provenance are in the repository README.

## What's New
### Batch Asset Downloads
* Added the ability to batch download covers, backgrounds, logos, and icons for your entire game library.
---
### New Customization Options
Take control of Tico's look and startup experience with several new personalization settings:
* **Skip the screen transition animation** for an instant switch between screens.
* **Customize the screen tint color**, affecting both the dock and the startup animation.
* **Change the tint color of inactive dock items** to better match your theme.
* **Customize the animated gradient border** with your preferred color.
* **Choose your startup screen**, launching directly into either **Home** or **Game Select**
---
### Homescreen & Backgrounds
* Added the option to use the game background as the homescreen background.
* Added per-screen homescreen backgrounds.
* Added a symbol decoration for console card home shortcuts.
* Added an optional background overlay for the homescreen — a semi-transparent white/black layer that improves the visibility of components above it.
* Added new background animations for Home and Game Select, which can be set individually per screen.
---
### Homescreen Cards
* Added styled console and game cards to the homescreen, each with a frame and badges available at all card sizes. Styled items can be disabled individually to show the raw item as before.
* Added **1×2** and **2×1** item size options, giving you more flexibility when organizing your layout.
---
### Interface Settings Refactor
The Interface settings have been reorganized into clearer sections:
* **Animations** — Skip animation, and Screen transition animation (used when the intro isn't skipped).
* **Screens** — Separate settings for Home (game backgrounds, background transition, theme overlay, and other previously available options) and Game Select (background transition, theme overlay, and other previously available options).
* **Card Settings** — Console and game card customization, now organized into sections, with a new option to extend card styling to the homescreen.
* **Tint** — Screen tint color, inactive dock item tint, and gradient border color.
---
### Interface & Navigation
* Improved the Quick Menu with per-screen options and a new layout.
* Improved the Retro Achievements screen layout, with a new per-console view.
* Added touch support to previously unsupported screens, including Assets and others.
* Added the option to rescan all consoles at once.
---
## Want to Contribute?

Every emulator core has its own repository under the **Tico GitHub organization**, making development, issue tracking, and contributions easier.

Bug reports, feature requests, and pull requests are always welcome. Please respect each core's original license and attribution requirements.

> [!WARNING]
> **Requires tico 0.8.0 or later.** This module doesn't work with older tico versions. If you're on an earlier version, wait for the tico 0.8.0 release before updating.

A big update: Dolphin is now a tico module. It gets the new in-game menu with every core option, button mapping, cheats, Riivolution mods, online play, auto save and per-game settings, and its saves move to tico's saves folder.

## Highlights

- **New quick menu**: the same menu as tico's other cores, with Save State, Load State, Change Disc, Cheats, Mods, Portal and Reset, plus a sidebar for Settings, Restart and Exit Game. It follows tico's theme and works by touch.
- **Full settings, in tico and in game**: every option the core supports, plus per-game settings (Settings › This Game).
- **Button mapping** (#7, #28, #44): Settings › Mapping remaps the GameCube Controller, Wii Remote (upright and sideways), Nunchuk and Classic Controller. **Shake**, **Tilt** and **Swing** can go on any button, for the Wii Remote and the Nunchuk.
- **Players screen**: Settings › Players shows the controller on each port and opens the Switch's controller screen.
- **Auto save and continue where you left off**, save states with pictures, Undo Load/Save State, and **Change Disc** for multi-disc games (states remember their disc).
- **Cheats** (#31): Gecko, Action Replay and patch codes in the Cheats menu, with **Download Gecko codes** for the running game.
- **Riivolution mods** (#22, #25): copy a mod's SD card files to `sdmc:/tico/mods/wii/`, then turn its options on in the quick menu's **Mods** screen and Restart.
- **Online play** (#14): the Wii now uses the Switch's internet connection, so games patched for **Wiimmfi** or **WiiLink WFC** can go online. Also **WiiConnect24 via WiiLink**, the GameCube **Broadband Adapter** with a choice of DNS, and **Correct time drift**.
- **Skylanders portal** (#39): Settings › System › Wii › Emulate Skylanders portal, then place figures from the quick menu's **Portal** screen. Figure dumps come from `sdmc:/tico/skylanders/` and from Emulanders' `sdmc:/emulanders/figures/`.
- **WiiWare and Virtual Console** (#4, #8): `.wad` files in the Wii list.
- **Triforce arcade games** (#42): a new Triforce system, `sdmc:/tico/roms/triforce/`. Coin is on −, Service on L3 and Test on R3.
- **Wii Menu and GameCube Menu** (#40): the first item in the Wii list once the Wii Menu is installed, and in the GameCube list once a GameCube BIOS is provided.
- **More formats** (#16): `.ciso` and `.gcz` games are listed.
- **Allow mismatched region settings** (#33): translated games can use the language you pick.
- **Boost mode**: Settings › Behavior › Boost mode (on by default) runs the CPU at 1785 MHz and the GPU at 768 MHz while you play.
- **deko3d renderer**: Dolphin now draws with deko3d, the Switch GPU's own API, from [nezumiiruka](https://github.com/PalindromicBreadLoaf/nezumiiruka) by @PalindromicBreadLoaf. Settings › Video › Renderer can switch to Vulkan if a game misbehaves on deko3d.
- **Game library**: opening Dolphin from the homebrew menu shows your GameCube and Wii games.

## Saves

- **Saves move to `sdmc:/tico/saves`** (#9), like the other cores: GameCube memory cards in `saves/gc/<region>`, each Wii game's save in `saves/wii/<GAMEID>`. Your existing saves are moved there on the first start, never over a save that's already there.
- **Wii save import** (#9): copy a Wii SD card's `private` folder (`data.bin` files) into `sdmc:/tico/saves/wii/import/`, and the save is imported when its game starts. The save it replaces is kept as a backup.
- **Wii save states** (#34): they now include the state of the Wii's system devices, which they used to miss. States made with older versions of Wii games won't load.

## Fixes

- **Boost clocks are kept** (#2): docking, undocking or waking from sleep no longer drops them back to stock. With **sys-clk**, **sys-clk-OC** (kefir) or **Horizon-OC**, Dolphin asks the clock manager for them instead of fighting

A big update: FinalBurn Neo is now a tico module. It renders with Vulkan, supports RetroArch slang shaders, shows vertical games upright and has its own game library. It also gets the new in-game menu with every core option, plus auto save, per-game settings and a Players screen.

## Highlights

- **New quick menu**: the same menu as tico's other cores. The list holds Save State, Load State and Reset, with a sidebar for Settings, Restart and Exit Game. Reset, Restart and Exit ask for confirmation, and tooltips explain the difference between Reset and Restart. The menu follows tico's light or dark theme, has the animated border in your Screen Colors tint, works by touch, and has an optional FPS / resolution display.
- **Vertical games shown upright** (#1): games made for a vertical monitor, such as 1942 or Arkanoid, now play upright with the Switch held normally. Settings › Video › Vertical mode still turns them for a Switch stood on its side (TATE).
- **Full settings, in tico and in game**: every global option the core supports, laid out in System, Display, Video, Audio, Input, Neo Geo and Controls tabs. That now includes the vector game resolution, the Neo Geo BIOS and memory card, and the full range of CPU clock and analog speed.
- **Per-game settings**: Settings › This Game › *Save current settings for this game* stores the game's own settings. From then on, changes apply to that game only. *Delete this game's settings* (asked first) brings back the shared ones. You can also manage them from tico: press **+** on a game in the launcher, or use Emulator Settings › Game Settings.
- **Players screen**: Settings › Players shows the controller each player has (Pro Controller, Joy-Con pair, handheld...). It also opens the Switch's controller screen to change who is which player.
- **Auto save and continue where you left off**: FinalBurn Neo saves your spot automatically when you exit, restart, return to the library or press HOME. Next time, it offers to continue from there, showing a picture and when it was saved. Choose *Ask*, *Always* or *Never* in tico › General › Continue Last Game.
- **Save states with pictures**: 5 slots plus the Auto slot. Each slot shows a picture of the game and when it was saved.

It also covers online games that have revival servers. Other players see your Switch user's name, or a nickname you choose. The console keeps the same PSP MAC address across launches, so servers and friend lists recognise it.
- **Frame generation (LSFG)**: Settings › Display › *Frame Generation* puts a generated frame between each two of a game's, so 30 fps games show 60. Games already at 60 fps are left alone. - **Buffer filtering** now changes how the picture is scaled; before, the option did nothing.
- **Settings that did nothing are gone**: hardware tessellation, software skinning, range culling and lazy texture caching (removed from PPSSPP), and frame skip type.
- **New options reach existing installs**: options added in an update are now written into your existing `ppsspp.jsonc`, so you no longer need to delete it (#7).
- **The PSP's clock follows the console's time zone.**
- **Hot Pixel's title screen** shows correctly (a compatibility fix from PPSSPP).
- **RetroAchievements over HTTPS**: logins and requests are now encrypted; before, they went over plain HTTP.

- Button mapping, ad hoc multiplayer and config defaults by **@jhuz0** (#4, #6, #7).

## Under the hood

- PPSSPP is now a self-contained tico module: settings, game list and translations ship with it.
- Translated into English, German, Spanish, French, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian and Chinese.

## Installing

Extract `tico-ppsspp-module.zip` into `sdmc:/tico/modules/` (you'll get `sdmc:/tico/modules/ppsspp/`).

**Upgrading from 2.x:**

> [!WARNING]
> **Requires tico 0.8.0 or later.** This module doesn't work with older tico versions. If you're on an earlier version, wait for the tico 0.8.0 release before updating.

A big update: Snes9x is now a tico module. It renders with Vulkan, supports RetroArch slang shaders, plays zipped games and has its own game library. It also gets the new in-game menu with every core option, plus cheats, auto save, per-game settings and a Players screen.

## Highlights

- **New quick menu**: the same menu as tico's other cores. The list holds Save State, Load State, Cheats and Reset, with a sidebar for Settings, Restart and Exit Game. Reset, Restart and Exit ask for confirmation, and tooltips explain the difference between Reset and Restart. The menu follows tico's light or dark theme, has the animated border in your Screen Colors tint, works by touch, and has an optional FPS / resolution display.
- **Full settings, in tico and in game**: every option the core supports. That now includes HD Mode 7 scaling and filtering, MSU-1 enhanced audio and the SuperFX timing model. An Advanced tab can hide background layers or sprites and set the volume of each sound channel.
- **Per-game settings**: Settings › This Game › *Save current settings for this game* stores the game's own settings. From then on, changes apply to that game only. *Delete this game's settings* (asked first) brings back the shared ones. You can also manage them from tico: press **+** on a game in the launcher, or use Emulator Settings › Game Settings.
- **Players screen**: Settings › Players shows the controller each player has (Pro Controller, Joy-Con pair, handheld...). It also opens the Switch's controller screen to change who is which player.
- **Auto save and continue where you left off**: Snes9x saves your spot automatically when you exit, restart, return to the library or press HOME. Next time, it offers to continue from there, showing a picture and when it was saved. Choose *Ask*, *Always* or *Never* in tico › General › Continue Last Game.
- **Save states with pictures**: 5 slots plus the Auto slot. Each slot shows a picture of the game and when it was saved.
- **Cheats**: Game Genie, Pro Action Replay and raw codes from RetroArch `.cht` or `.cheats` files in `sdmc:/tico/cheats/snes/`. Every cheat is off at launch.
- **RetroArch slang shaders**: Settings › Shaders lets you browse presets in `sdmc:/tico/shaders/` and tune each shader's parameters. Built in: xBRZ, Eagle and CRT Easy Mode.
- **Vulkan rendering**: Snes9x now draws through Vulkan.
- **Button mapping**: a new Controls tab assigns every SNES button to any Switch button, with an option to use the left stick as the D-pad. The mapping applies to all four controllers.
- **Configurable fast forward**: choose 150%, 200%, 300%, 400% or unlimited speed, hold or toggle, and which button triggers it.
- **Zipped games**: play games straight from `.zip`, `.7z` and `.rar` archives. Saves are named after the archive, so `Chrono Trigger.zip` and `Chrono Trigger.sfc` share the same save.
- **Game library**: opening Snes9x from the homebrew menu shows a list of your SNES games, with access to Settings.
- **Multiple ROM folders**: Snes9x finds games in all of tico's ROM base folders. You can also add folders in Settings › Library (up to 16), then change, reorder or remove them.
- **USB drives**: play games from USB drives (FAT32/exFAT; NTFS read-only).

## Save safety

- Saves, clocks and states are written to a temporary file first, then put in place. A crash or a full SD card mid-write keeps the old file.
- Game saves keep their last 3 versions in `backups/`. Each state slot keeps the state it held before you saved over it.

## Fixes

- **PAL games run at the right speed**: 50 Hz games no longer run 20% too fast.
- **Real-time clock games keep their clock**: the S-RTC and SPC7110 clocks (Daikaijuu Monogatari II, Far East of Eden Zero) are now saved next to your game save.
- Smoother frame pacing, with less stuttering.

# The Minish Cap — Nintendo Switch (native homebrew) · USA + PT‑BR

Native **Nintendo Switch** homebrew builds of the Minish Cap PC‑decompilation port — a **native recompilation** (it runs on the Switch's own CPU with a software PPU/APU; **it is not an emulator**). Two builds:

- 🇺🇸 **USA** — original English.
- 🇧🇷 **BR (PT‑BR)** — Brazilian Portuguese translation (*romsportugues* "T1.0‑Final") + Portuguese overlay UI by default.

> ⚠️ **No game data is included.** The `.nro` ships only the engine + a pre‑baked asset cache. You must provide your **own legally‑dumped GBA ROM** — it supplies the actual game data.

## ✨ What's included in these builds
- 🏆 **RetroAchievements** — full `rcheevos` / `rc_client` integration over HTTPS, with a styled in‑game unlock overlay (issue #12).
- ⚡ **GPU renderer (OpenGL ES 2)** — runs **60 fps without overclocking**.
- 🎮 **Controls** — A/B mapped to Nintendo's physical face‑button layout, analog‑stick support.
- 🔤 **On‑screen menu** — scaled overlay/settings (Minus button), FPS‑counter options, multilingual (EN / PT / ES).
- 📂 **Loads any `*.gba` by content**, not by filename — so a translation hack works as‑is.
- 🛠️ Opt‑in frame profiler; clean RELEASE build (no per‑frame SD logging).

---

- A Nintendo Switch with custom firmware (**Atmosphère**) and the **Homebrew Menu** (hbmenu).

| Build | ROM you need | SHA‑1 of the ROM |
|---|---|---|
| **USA** | The Legend of Zelda: The Minish Cap (USA) | `b4bd50e4131b027c334547b4524e2dbbd4227130` |
| **BR / PT‑BR** | Minish Cap PT‑BR translation — *romsportugues T1.0‑Final* | `6838e0405c1be5d867d84e019d1f131a366b07ad` |

> ⚠️ **One ROM at a time.** Both builds read `/switch/tmc/baserom.gba`. To switch between USA and BR, replace `baserom.gba` with the matching ROM **and delete the folder `/switch/tmc/assets/`** so the cache rebuilds for the new ROM.

## torchlight-nx 1.0.2

A performance update: the game runs noticeably smoother, still at the console's **stock clocks** and with exactly
the same picture as before. **To update:** replace `sdmc:/switch/torchlight/torchlight.nro` with the one from the
zip. Your game files, saves and settings stay where they are.

### Faster

The port is limited by the game's main thread, which runs the whole OGRE engine and the game logic on one CPU core.
This version makes that thread do the same work in less time, so the frame rate is higher in town and in the dungeons.

- **Better compiled game code.** The recompiled code of the game is now rewritten at build time before being
  compiled: function calls that go through a table but almost always reach the same function become direct calls,
  constants that the game only reads are built into the code, floating-point values are loaded more efficiently
  on the Switch's CPU, and short functions and loops keep the game's registers in the CPU instead of memory. These
  rewrites come from the [sa2-nx](https://github.com/ChanseyIsTheBest/sa2-nx) port by ChanseyIsTheBest.
- **More of the engine in native code.** A few of the engine's busiest functions now run as native code written for
  the port: the search for visible objects in the scene, the animated effects updated every frame (textures and
  particle timers), and the measurement of text width used to lay out text. Every one of them was checked against
  the game's own code to give bit-for-bit the same results.
- **Smoother dialogs.** Laying out long texts, such as quest dialogs, was especially slow: some scenes with a quest
  giver dropped the frame rate a lot. Text layout is now much faster.
- **Lighter renderer bookkeeping.** The work the port does on the main thread to hand each frame over to the Vulkan
  renderer waits less on memory.

Nothing changes in the rendering: no frames skipped, no effects reduced. Overclocking stays optional.

### Installation

Unchanged: see the README. You need your own copy of the Xbox Live Arcade game (its package from your Xbox 360).

packages.changelog:
# Zelda Save Editor 0.1.5-alpha.5

Public prerelease by StockiestThree9. This update retains BOTW support and adds the TOTK development work completed since 0.1.4-beta.1.

## Changes since the store beta

- Experimental Tears of the Kingdom save discovery and editing, with player values, stamina wheels, battery cells, abilities and pouch capacity.
- Grouped item selection: choose an armor family, then its stars and supported style. Hylian Hood up/down is independent of rank. Weapons offer verified Decayed/Pristine and appearance choices. Search and category filters shorten the lists.
- Inventory add/replace/remove/equip, fusion choices, durability repair, armor upgrades, pristine conversion, meal effects and bulk stack tools.
- Registered horses, world/completion flags, compendium states, direct quest stages, map stamps and daily amiibo reset.
- Autobuild slot/favorite management and import/export using this editor's checksummed `.zsbp` format.
- BOTW inventory validation improvements, stale-selection protection after undo/redo, faster change tracking and clearer menu flows.

Game names, item relationships and other resource tables are read from the user's installed game and cached privately. No Nintendo resource cache, save, font or audio sample is distributed.

## Install or update

Extract `Zelda-Save-Editor-v0.1.5-alpha.5.zip` at the SD root, preserving existing files. The executable remains `/switch/Zelda_Save_Editor.nro`; documentation and notices are under `/switch/zelda-save-editor/`. Existing saves, backups, cache, settings and blueprints are not included or replaced by the package. A standalone NRO and a source archive including libpulsar are also provided.

Launch Sphaira in full application mode by holding R while opening the relevant game, then launch Zelda Save Editor. Close the actual game before editing its save. Settings → Game resources can retry loading the installed resources.

## Testing and current limits

Rechecked on 19 October 2026: native Switch build; 495 synthetic/core checks; 580 BOTW real-fixture checks; 7,090 TOTK checks with a real fixture and installed 1.4.3 resources; storage/backup/conflict checks; 230 BOTW normal-profile-swap checks; and both host UI walkthroughs.

This is still an **alpha for TOTK**. Host checks do not establish that every edited save is valid in-game. Gameplay acceptance of the expanded edits and resource loading on a fresh console installation remain unverified. Only one accepted TOTK save revision has a real test fixture. Keep an independent backup and begin with a small edit before testing broader changes.

World/quest edits change saved fields without reconciling all related story events or rewards. Graphical maps, sparse object completion such as individual bosses/Addison signs, full horse creation/customization and community Autobuild formats are not implemented. BOTW profile swapping excludes Master Mode; gameplay after swaps still needs wider device testing.

See [TOTK feature details and limits](https://github.com/amarkham23/Zelda-Save-Editor/blob/v0.1.5-alpha.5/docs/TOTK-ALPHA.md), [full changes](https://github.com/amarkham23/Zelda-Save-Editor/blob/v0.1.5-alpha.5/docs/CHANGES.md), and [BOTW profile-swap behavior](https://github.com/amarkham23/Zelda-Save-Editor/blob/v0.1.5-alpha.5/docs/PROFILE-SWAPS.md).

packages.changelog:
# ZERODROID v1.0.1 — Official Launch Release / Versión Oficial de Lanzamiento

## [ES] Español

### 🎮 ZERODROID v1.0.1: Cliente No Oficial de Boosteroid para Nintendo Switch

`ZERODROID_v1.0.1.nro` es la versión oficial de lanzamiento de ZERODROID, diseñada desde cero para ofrecer la experiencia completa de Boosteroid en Nintendo Switch con interfaz gráfica nativa a 60 FPS, aceleración de video H.264 por hardware NVDEC, decodificación de audio Opus y controles personalizados.

---

### ✨ Novedades Principales de la v1.0.1

1. **Carátulas y Posteres en Alta Definición:**
   * Reemplazo de marcos anchos con barras laterales por ranuras verticales tipo póster (`v101-poster` / `v101-banner`), con recorte centrado automático y marco azul marino sin deformación.
2. **Biblioteca Paginada y Navegación Intuitiva:**
   * Navegación completa por pestañas: **Mis juegos**, **Catálogo**, **Favoritos** y **Recientes**.
   * Búsqueda nativa, filtrado por estados de licencia (Gratuito, Requiere licencia, Instalar y Jugar) y favoritos persistentes.
   * Navegación fluida mediante botones de control (**ZL/ZR** para secciones, **L/R** para páginas) y pantalla táctil nativa.
3. **Centro de Control e Interfaz de Transmisión:**
   * Acceso rápido mediante el botón **X lila** táctil superior derecho.
   * Acciones rápidas: **Xbox Guide**, **Steam Menu** (`Shift + Tab`), **ALT+TAB**, **Keyboard Info**, **Mouse Virtual / Trackpad**, **Reconexión UDP**, **Ajustes Gráficos** y **Volver al Juego**.
   * Cursor virtual lila de GPU deko3d con auto-ocultado tras 3 segundos de inactividad.
4. **Perfiles de Imagen y Resoluciones:**
   * Soporte para modos **Auto** (720p portátil / 1080p dock), **720p**, **1080p** y **1440p experimental**.
   * Perfiles de color: *Natural*, *Nítido (Sharp)*, *Vivo*, *Cine*, *Suave* y *Personalizado*.

---

### 💻 Instalación en Nintendo Switch

1. Descarga los archivos `ZERODROID_v1.0.1.nro` y `ZERODROID_v1.0.1.sha256`.
2. Copia el binario a tu tarjeta SD en `sdmc:/switch/ZERODROID/ZERODROID.nro`.
3. Inicia Homebrew Menu en modo **Title Takeover**: mantén presionado **R** mientras inicias cualquier juego instalado en tu consola.
   *(Nota: No uses el modo Álbum/Applet Mode, ya que no otorga la memoria RAM necesaria para la decodificación de video y red WebRTC)*.

---

## [EN] English

### 🎮 ZERODROID v1.0.1: Unofficial Boosteroid Client for Nintendo Switch

`ZERODROID_v1.0.1.nro` is the first complete official launch release of ZERODROID, tailored specifically for Nintendo Switch homebrew with native 60 FPS rendering, NVDEC hardware H.264 video decoding, Opus audio playback, and customizable streaming profiles.

---

### ✨ Key Features & Improvements in v1.0.1

1. **High-Definition Poster Artwork:**
   * Replaced letterboxed card artwork with vertical poster slots (`v101-poster` / `v101-banner`), featuring centered source crop and slim navy borders. Cover art is never stretched or distorted.
2. **Complete Paginated Library & Touch Navigation:**
   * Full tabbed browsing: **My Games**, **Catalog**, **Favorites**, and **Recent**.
   * Native search bar, license badges (*Free*, *License Required*, *Install & Play*), and persistent favorites.
   * Dual controller (**ZL/ZR** for section switching, **L/R** for pagination) and release-on-tap Switch touch navigation.
3. **In-Stream Control Center (Top-Right Purple X):**
   * Accessible in-game via the top-right purple X touch overlay.
   * Actions: **Xbox Guide**, **Steam Menu** (`Shift + Tab`), **ALT+TAB**, **Keyboard Info**, **Virtual Mouse / Trackpad**, **UDP Reconnection**, **Graphic Presets**, and **Return to Game**.
   * Hardware-rendered purple virtual cursor via deko3d GPU quad with 3-second auto-hide.
4. **Resolution Modes & Image Profiles:**
   * Resolution selector: **Auto** (720p handheld / 1080p docked), **720p**, **1080p**, and **1440p experimental**.
   * Preset color profiles: *Natural*, *Sharp*, *Vivid*, *Cinema*, *Soft*, and *Custom*.

---
